docs.title: Chat
docs.summary: Per-circle text chat. Every circle member can read and post; nobody else can (a non-member gets 404, the same as an unknown circle). This page describes the readable (Normal circle) chat; in a…
docs.text: Chat Per-circle text chat. Every circle member can read and post; nobody else can (a non-member gets 404, the same as an unknown circle). This page describes the readable (Normal circle) chat; in a Private circle chat is end-to-end encrypted, see Encrypted chat. API Endpoint Purpose GET /circles/{id}/chat?before=<seq>&limit=<n> Newest-first page (default 50, max 100). nextbefore is the cursor for the next older page, null at the start of history. POST /circles/{id}/chat {"body": "..."} Send. Returns 201 with the stored message. POST /circles/{id}/chat/read {"seq": n} Mark read up to seq (omit for newest). Clamped to the newest message; never moves backwards. GET /circles/{id}/chat?after=<seq> Catch-up: only messages newer than seq (used after a socket reconnect). POST /circles/{id}/chat {"body", "clientid"?} With a clientid (max 64 chars) a retry returns the already stored message (200, no duplicate, no second push). PATCH /circles/{id}/chat/{msgId} {"body"} Edit your own message (photo captions too). Others get 404. Sets editedat; live chatedit frame. DELETE /circles/{id}/chat/{msgId} Hard-delete (row, text and photo). Sender, or a circle admin (moderation, audit-logged as chat.delete). Live chatdelete frame. POST /circles/{id}/chat/photo Photo message (JPEG/PNG, 5 MiB, re-encoded to drop EXIF). GET .../{msgId}/photo serves it to members only. GET /chat/unread {"circles": {id: n}, "total": n}, other people's messages newer than your read marker. Limits: body is trimmed, 1 to 2000 characters (413 above that), at most 20 sends per user per minute (429). Messages live in chatmessages (migration 000110) and are deleted with their circle or sender. Live delivery and push A send is broadcast as a WebSocket frame {"type":"chat","circleid":...,"message":{...}} to every socket subscribed to the circle, over the existing /ws/stream hub. Other members' devices also get a push (direct, UnifiedPush or APNs). The push never carries location data and, unless VERBOSEPUSH=true, not the message text either: it reads "New message in <circle>". App The Circle tab has a Chat row (and the tab icon a badge) showing the unread count. The chat screen shows the message list, loads older pages on scroll, and has a composer that refuses empty or over-long text. Long-press a bubble in the app to edit or delete (admins see delete on any message). A failed send keeps the draft and retries with the same clientid. The open chat fetches missed messages on every WebSocket reconnect. Sends, edits and deletes share the 20 per minute limit (migration 000210 adds editedat and clientid). Privacy and E2EE Normal circles. Chat is stored as plain text on your Orbitly server, as described above. Push text is content-free unless the recipient opted in. Removed members lose read, post and photo access immediately; deleting a message removes it from the database (backups age out per retention). Private (end-to-end encrypted) circles. Chat is encrypted on the sender's phone and can only be opened on the phones of people in the circle. The server relays scrambled data it cannot read, and never gives the chat key to the server's own processing helper, even for members who chose "server processing" for their location. Full design: design/E2EECHAT.md. What that means in practice: The chat screen shows "Encrypted. Only people in this circle can read this." Messages, edits, deletes and photos all work as before. Photos are encrypted with their own key before upload. Sending works offline: messages wait on your phone and go out later. A message that could not be delivered says "Not sent. Tap to try again." Notifications are made on your phone after it decrypts the message. The server only wakes your phone ("something is waiting"); it never carries message text or even who wrote it. If your phone is switched off or the system delays the wake-up, you see the message when you next open the app. The server still knows that a message was sent, from which phone (so which person), when (to the minute) and a rough size. It cannot tell a message from an edit or a delete, and it cannot read anything inside. The unread badge is counted on your phone. The server's own count (used only as a fallback) can be a little high because it cannot tell edits from messages. Only the author can edit a message. The author or a circle admin can delete it; every phone checks this itself. The server keeps the encrypted copies for 30 days (the server owner can change this with E2EECHATTTLDAYS, 1 to 365). Your phone keeps its own history (the last 5000 messages per circle), so older chat stays on phones that already had it. A reinstalled or new phone can only restore what is still on the server. People who leave the circle cannot read anything sent after they left. A newly joined person can read recent messages still stored on the server (up to 30 days) that were sealed with the key they received. Ask an admin to make a new circle key before inviting if that matters. A family member whose app is too old cannot read or send encrypted chat; the chat screen says "<name> needs to update Orbitly to read encrypted chat." and an old app that tries to send gets the message "Chat in this circle is end-to-end encrypted. Update Orbitly to send and read new messages." When a circle turns private. Messages written before that stay on the server as readable text. They remain visible, marked "Sent before encryption". A circle admin can remove them for good with "Delete them" in the chat banner (DELETE /circles/{id}/chat/history). API additions: 409 {"code":"chatencrypted"} for plaintext send, edit and photo in a private circle; POST /circles/{id}/chat/read {"itemid": n}; DELETE /circles/{id}/chat/history (admin); POST /circles/{id}/e2ee/blobs, GET /circles/{id}/e2ee/blobs/{id} for encrypted photos; GET /circles/{id}/chat answers "encrypted": true for a private circle (the list is then only the old plaintext history). Not supported Reactions, typing indicators, per-message location sharing. In normal circles offline queueing of unsent messages across app restarts (the draft survives only while the screen is open) and a deletion missed while offline is corrected the next time the chat is opened. In private circles read receipts ("Seen by") are not available, and sending a photo needs a connection (the text of a message does not).

docs.title: Safety alerts: what Orbitly does
docs.summary: Orbitly notifies your family. It never contacts emergency services (no 911/112/999 call, no dispatch). If someone is in danger, call your local emergency number first.
docs.text: Safety alerts: what Orbitly does Orbitly notifies your family. It never contacts emergency services (no 911/112/999 call, no dispatch). If someone is in danger, call your local emergency number first. What happens Action Family push Family live (WebSocket) SMS to the sender's emergency contacts Check-in yes yes no (opt-in: ALERTSMSONCHECKIN) Help yes yes no (opt-in: ALERTSMSONCHECKIN) SOS yes yes yes, up to the limits below SMS goes only to emergency contacts the sender added themselves, never to phone numbers on other members' profiles, and only when Twilio is configured. The SMS says the family was notified and that emergency services have not been contacted. It never contains coordinates. If PUBLICBASEURL is https it carries a temporary link to a no-script page showing the last known position; otherwise it carries no location. Push payloads never contain coordinates. Unless VERBOSEPUSH=true they also omit the sender's name and the free-text note ("A family member sent SOS"). The API response to the sender states: "Your family has been notified. Emergency services were not contacted." Every alert writes an alert.<type> audit entry, plus an alert.fanout summary (counts only). Delivery states GET /alerts/{id} (sender or an admin of the sender's family) returns one row per recipient and channel (push, ws, sms): State Meaning queued accepted by the server, not yet handed to a provider (for direct push: waiting for the phone to connect) sent the provider accepted it (ntfy/APNs for push, Twilio API for SMS). This is not proof the phone received it delivered queued onto the recipient's live WebSocket (ws), or acknowledged by the phone over the built-in direct push channel (push; see push.md) failed see error: invalidphone, providererror, rejectedbyprovider, smsnotconfigured, or a limit code acknowledged the recipient confirmed with POST /alerts/{id}/ack Twilio delivery-status callbacks are not used, so SMS stops at sent/failed. The first acknowledgement reaches the sender as a WebSocket frame {"type":"alertack", "alertid", "userid", "name", "acknowledgedat"}. Acks are idempotent. A ws row exists only for members who were connected. GET /alerts?limit=&before= lists the caller's family history, newest first (limit 1-100, default 20; before is the last id of the previous page; nextbefore is empty on the last page). Coordinates appear only on active alerts. Limits (environment variables) Variable Default Effect ALERTSOSCOOLDOWN 2m gap between two SOS from one user (429) ALERTCOOLDOWN 1m gap between two check-in/help from one user ALERTFAMILYMAXPERHOUR 30 check-in/help per family per hour (429). SOS is never refused ALERTSMSMAXRECIPIENTS 5 contacts texted per alert; the rest are failed: limitrecipientsperalert ALERTSMSSENDERPERDAY 10 SMS per sender per 24 h (counted in the database) ALERTSMSFAMILYPERHOUR 20 SMS per family per hour ALERTSMSONCHECKIN false also SMS contacts for check-in/help ALERTSHARETTL 4h location-link lifetime, max 7 days The two cooldowns are in memory and reset on restart. A limit only suppresses SMS; push and live delivery to the family always happen. Share links 128-bit random tokens, expire after ALERTSHARETTL, can be turned off at any time with POST /alerts/{id}/share/revoke (then HTTP 410), stop showing the location once the alert is resolved, and are served with no-store, noindex, no-referrer and a CSP that forbids scripts and third-party loads.

docs.title: Check-ins and temporary sharing
docs.summary: Three small features that let a person decide, for a limited time, who sees where they are. Orbitly still never contacts emergency services (see safety.md); none of this changes SOS.
docs.text: Check-ins and temporary sharing Three small features that let a person decide, for a limited time, who sees where they are. Orbitly still never contacts emergency services (see safety.md); none of this changes SOS. "I'm here" check-in to chosen people POST /checkins {recipientids, note?, lat?, lon?} Every recipient must share at least one circle with the sender. Anyone else (or an unknown id) gives a uniform 404 member not found. Up to 25 recipients, note up to 280 characters, lat/lon together and in range. Sender cooldown is ALERTCOOLDOWN. Stored in checkins / checkinrecipients for 30 days (expiresat). Reads filter on expiresat > now(); expired rows are also deleted opportunistically. Delivered over the recipients' WebSocket ({"type":"checkin", ...}) and push. Like other pushes it carries no coordinates and, unless VERBOSEPUSH=true, neither the sender's name nor the note. GET /checkins lists check-ins you received; ?direction=sent lists yours. limit 1-100 (default 30). A check-in is an explicit act, so it works while sharing is paused. Audit entry checkin.send (counts only). This is separate from the family-wide POST /alerts/check-in. Pause sharing PUT /sharing/pause with exactly one of {minutes} or {until: RFC3339} (1 minute to 30 days from now); GET /sharing/pause; DELETE /sharing/pause resumes at once. The app offers 1 hour, until tomorrow (07:00 local) and custom. The pause is folded into every sharing decision in internal/circles (SharedWith, SharingCircles, OwnAndSharingCircles, LocationVisibility, MemberCircles), so it is honoured by the members snapshot, the live WebSocket broadcast and presence frames, POST /locations/watch (live boost, which returns the usual 404) and the trips endpoints. pauseduntil > now() is evaluated in SQL on each read: a pause ends on time without any job. Setting or clearing a pause sends the usual sharing frame (with paused/pauseduntil) to circle- aware clients; expiry sends no frame, clients pick the pin up on the next location frame or snapshot. The phone keeps recording its own history and geofences while paused. SOS (/alerts/sos) does not use these helpers and always shares. Platform-admin consoles are outside circles and are not affected. Live share with one person POST /live-shares {viewerid, minutes} (1 to 1440) shares your last known position with one circle member until it expires; re-sharing replaces the expiry. GET /live-shares returns {outgoing, incoming}; incoming entries carry the sharer's last position and recordedat, withheld (paused: true) while the sharer's sharing is paused. DELETE /live-shares/{id} ends it (either party). Expiry is checked on every read, and membership is re-checked on read, so leaving the circle ends the share. Viewers poll GET /live-shares; live shares are not pushed over the WebSocket.

docs.title: Share links ("share your live location with anyone")
docs.summary: A person can mint a link that anyone can open in a browser, with no app and no account, to follow their live location until it expires or is stopped.
docs.text: Share links ("share your live location with anyone") A person can mint a link that anyone can open in a browser, with no app and no account, to follow their live location until it expires or is stopped. Endpoints Authenticated: POST /share-links {minutes (1..4320), label?} returns {id, url, token, createdat, expiresat, label}. The token (256 random bits, base64url) and url (PublicBaseURL or the request host, plus /s/<token>) appear only in this response. At most 10 active links per user (409), 30 creations per hour. GET /share-links lists the caller's active links (no token). DELETE /share-links/{id} stops sharing at once (uniform 404 for anything that is not the caller's active link). Public, unauthenticated: GET /s/{token} the self-contained viewer page. GET /s/{token}/data JSON the page polls every 5 s while visible: state (active paused nolocation), name, initial, photourl?, lat, lon, accuracym, headingdeg, speedmps, batterypct, updatedat, expiresat. Nothing else: no id, email, circle, or history. While the owner's sharing is paused, state is paused and no location or battery is returned. GET /s/{token}/photo the owner's avatar while the link is live. Storage and hardening Table sharelinks (migration 000112) stores SHA-256(token) only. Unknown, malformed, expired and revoked tokens give the same generic 404 (identical body), so a response never reveals which. Expiry and revocation are evaluated in SQL on every request; the viewer stops immediately. Lookup is by hash (index key) and the stored hash is re-compared in constant time. Per-IP rate limits: 150 requests/min, and 30 misses per 15 min (429). Headers: Cache-Control: no-store, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nosniff, frame denial, and a CSP of default-src 'none' with a nonce for the one inline script, connect-src 'self', and img-src 'self' data: plus the operator's tile host. Map tiles and privacy The page loads no CDN script or font. Its map is a small slippy-map written in the page itself, drawing raster tiles from the same TILEURL that /config advertises (must be https; default OpenStreetMap). The viewer's browser therefore contacts that tile host, which sees the viewer's IP and the area viewed. Tile images are requested with referrerpolicy=origin, so the tile host gets this server's origin but never the secret path. To keep tile traffic on your own infrastructure, point TILEURL at a self-hosted tile server (see maps.md). Vector styles (MAPSTYLEURL) are not used by the page.

docs.title: Geofence alert thresholds
docs.summary: Arrival and departure alerts are evaluated server-side after each stored fix (handlers/geofenceeval.go). Two layers keep GPS drift from raising false alerts:
docs.text: Geofence alert thresholds Arrival and departure alerts are evaluated server-side after each stored fix (handlers/geofenceeval.go). Two layers keep GPS drift from raising false alerts: 1. Accuracy gate. A fix whose reported horizontal accuracy is worse than geofenceMaxAccuracyMeters (100 m) is stored and shown on the map but never drives a transition (no enter, no exit, no pending transition). A fix with no accuracy value is trusted. The periodic reconcile pass applies the same gate to the last known position. 2. Debounce. A transition is notified at most once per geofenceDebounceInterval (60 s) per geofence and user. A transition inside the window becomes pending; if the user is back in the previously notified state before it fires, the pair is dropped, otherwise it fires once the window elapses (reconcile runs every 60 s). Stationary jitter additionally dedups at ingest (stationaryDedupMeters 10 m, widened to 25 m for poor-accuracy fixes) so a parked phone does not write rows or flip state. Tests: TestGeofenceFixUsable, TestGeofenceNoAlertOnLowAccuracyDrift (a low-accuracy drift burst produces zero events, one accurate departure produces exactly one).

docs.title: Bubbles
docs.summary: A Bubble is a temporary, per-person geofence modelled on Life360's "Create Bubble". From a member's profile you tap Create Bubble, size a circle around where that person is right now with a slider…
docs.text: Bubbles A Bubble is a temporary, per-person geofence modelled on Life360's "Create Bubble". From a member's profile you tap Create Bubble, size a circle around where that person is right now with a slider, pick how long it lasts (1 hour, 4 hours, until tonight, 24 hours), and confirm. You are alerted when they leave the circle (optionally also when they come back). It then expires and is deleted server-side. API All routes need a signed-in user. Route Effect POST /bubbles {subjectid, radiusm, durationminutes, notifyreenter} Creates a Bubble. radiusm 50-5000, durationminutes 15-1440. 201 with the Bubble GET /bubbles {"bubbles": [...], "aboutme": [...]}: your active Bubbles (with the circle) and the active ones other people drew around you (creator and expiry only) DELETE /bubbles/{id} Cancels a Bubble. Creator only; anyone else gets 404 Errors: 400 bad input (including a Bubble on yourself), 404 subject is not a circle co-member who is sharing with you right now (one uniform answer, so membership and pauses cannot be probed), 409 the subject has no position newer than 30 minutes, 429 more than 10 active Bubbles. Creating a second Bubble on the same person replaces the first. Privacy rules The creator and subject must share a circle in which the subject currently shares their location (circles.SharedWith: sharing on, no pause). A person who has paused sharing cannot be bubbled. The centre is the subject's last server-side position. The client never supplies coordinates, so a Bubble cannot be used to probe a place. The subject is told. On creation they get a push "A family member created a Bubble around you until HH:MM" (the creator's name only with VERBOSEPUSH, like every other push; time in the zone they set for quiet hours, else UTC), and GET /bubbles lists it under aboutme. They never receive coordinates or the radius, and cannot see the circle on a map. The circle is returned only to the creator and drawn only on the creator's map. The subject cannot cancel it; the control they have is the one they already have: pausing or switching off sharing. While paused (or not sharing with the creator) a Bubble is not evaluated at all: no alert and no state change, so nothing about their movement leaks. Push payloads never contain coordinates. Evaluation evaluateBubbles runs at the top of evaluateGeofences, so it sees every stored point (ingest, batch upload, and the 60 s reconcile loop that re-checks each active user's latest point). A Bubble starts "inside". Leaving is crossing the radius; coming back is crossing 90% of it, so a fix jittering on the edge does not flap. A transition is claimed with a conditional UPDATE, so two concurrent evaluations of one point alert once, and re-evaluating the same point is a no-op. Points older than the Bubble itself are ignored. An alert goes to the creator only: a {"type":"bubble","event":"leftentered", "bubbleid","userid","name"} WebSocket frame and a push through the shared pushUsers pipeline (direct, UnifiedPush, APNs). Bubble alerts are not rows in alerts (that table is for SOS/help/check-in and has no recipient-delivery semantics for this), so they have no alertdeliveries tracking. Expiry Reads ignore rows past expiresat. They are deleted by the geofence reconcile loop (purgeExpiredBubbles, every minute) and by purgeExpiredSharing on create. Storage Migration 000113bubbles: table bubbles (circleid, creatorid, subjectid, lat, lon, radiusm, notifyreenter, expiresat, lastinside, lasteventat, createdat); rows cascade when the circle or either user is deleted.

docs.title: Driving events and the weekly driving report
docs.summary: Orbitly detects three kinds of driving risk events on the server, from the GPS fixes that already make up a trip, and summarises them per week or month for the people in a circle.
docs.text: Driving events and the weekly driving report Orbitly detects three kinds of driving risk events on the server, from the GPS fixes that already make up a trip, and summarises them per week or month for the people in a circle. Kind Meaning Magnitude speeding Speed above the limit for a sustained time max speed, m/s hardbrake Sudden deceleration while moving m/s^2 (positive) rapidaccel Sudden acceleration to a moving speed m/s^2 phoneuse Phone handled while driving. Only from the phone (below), and only for members who turned on the separate phone-use opt-in; null in reports (shown as Off in the app, never 0) for everyone else interaction duration, s Events only exist inside legs classified as driving (walking, cycling and slow transit never produce events). How events are detected Code: backend/internal/trips/events.go (pure functions, unit tested with synthetic tracks). The fixes are cleaned first (out-of-order, duplicate, inaccurate and teleporting fixes are dropped), then: Speeding: consecutive fixes whose speed is above the limit, at most 15 s apart, lasting at least the minimum duration (first to last over-limit fix). One event per sustained episode, with start, end and max speed. Hard brake / rapid acceleration: acceleration is computed only between two consecutive fixes at most 4 s apart (and at least 0.5 s), both with accuracy of 30 m or better, using the GPS speed (distance / time only when the device did not report a speed). Braking needs the vehicle above about 5 m/s before the interval, acceleration needs it above 5 m/s after. Intervals implying more than 12 m/s^2 are GPS jumps and are ignored. Adjacent qualifying intervals of the same kind merge into one event. Events are replaced together with their trip (same transaction), so recomputing with POST /trips/compute is idempotent. New trips get events from the background job; to add events to older trips, recompute the range. Thresholds Env Default Meaning DRIVINGSPEEDINGMPS 35.76 Speeding limit, m/s (80 mph) DRIVINGSPEEDINGSECONDS 30 Minimum duration above the limit DRIVINGHARDBRAKEMPS2 3.5 Deceleration magnitude of a hard brake DRIVINGRAPIDACCELMPS2 3.5 Acceleration of a rapid start Empty, non-numeric or zero values fall back to the defaults. The thresholds in effect are returned in the report (thresholds). The older per-request speedthresholdmps of GET /trips/summary is independent and unchanged. API GET /trips/report?period=weekmonth&start=YYYY-MM-DD&utcoffsetminutes=&circleid= Weeks start on Monday in the caller's local time (local date derived from utcoffsetminutes, default 0); start selects any week or month (snapped to its start). circleid defaults to the caller's primary circle. Returns totals, previoustotals, per-member events and previousevents, thresholds and estimated: true. Members include everyone the viewer may see, also those with zero drives. Distances are in metres and speeds in m/s; clients convert. Also returns (additive): days: one {date:"YYYY-MM-DD", drives, distancem, topspeedmps} per local calendar day of the period (7 for a week, 28-31 for a month), zero filled, with days cut at the caller's utcoffsetminutes. recenttrips: up to 10 driving trips of the period across the visible members, newest first: {id, userid, name, startedat, endedat, distancem, durations, maxspeedmps, mode, eventcounts:{speeding, hardbrake, rapidaccel, phoneuse}}. eventcounts.phoneuse is null unless that member has phone-use detection on. Event counts follow the same "sensor wins" view as the report. Both use exactly the report's authorization: circle membership plus the member sharing location (a member always sees their own trips). GET /trips/{id}/events lists a trip's events. GET /trips/{id} includes the same list as events. Reviewing events (owner only) PUT /trips/{id}/passenger {"passenger":truefalse}: mark the drive "I was a passenger". Its events leave reports, scores and the weekly summary. The mark is kept per (user, trip start) so it survives trip recomputation. PATCH /trips/events/{eventId} {"dismissed":truefalse}: mark one phoneuse event as a false alarm. Same effect. Anyone else, an unknown id or a non-phone-use event gets 404. GET /trips/{id} and /trips/{id}/events add passenger, and event rows add maxspeedmps, confidence, activity and dismissed (dismissed events are listed only to their owner so they can be restored). Phone sensor events The Android app can detect hardbrake and rapidaccel with the motion sensor, and phoneuse (a separate, experimental switch that stays off by default), and upload them. Driving detection is on by default in the app: the app sends the opt-in (sensorenabled=true) the first time it can and retries until acknowledged; turn it off in Settings > Driving detection. The opt-in is per user, not per device, and is stored in users.drivingsensorenabled (server default false until the app reports). Phone-use detection has its own opt-in, users.drivingphoneuseenabled (migration 000103, default false, requires the sensor opt-in), because the server cannot know it from sensorenabled. POST /trips/sensor-events Authenticated exactly like POST /locations: X-Device-Key: <deviceid>.<key> (bound to its device and user; a body naming another deviceid is 403) or a normal Bearer access token. Body, at most 64 KB (413 above): {"events":[{"kind":"hardbrake","startedat":"2026-10-21T12:00:00Z", "endedat":"2026-10-21T12:00:02Z","magnitude":4.2, "lat":40.1,"lon":-75.2}], "sensorenabled": true, "phoneuseenabled": false} kind: hardbrake, rapidaccel or phoneuse. startedat / endedat: RFC3339; start within the last 7 days and at most 5 minutes in the future; end not before start, duration at most 5 minutes. magnitude: m/s^2 in 0-30 for braking and acceleration; for phoneuse the interaction duration in seconds, 0-300. lat / lon: both or neither (null), within -90..90 / -180..180. phoneuse only, all optional: maxspeedmps (0-100), confidence (0-1; out of range rejects the event), activity (screen or call; anything else is ignored). At most 100 events per request (400 above). events may be empty when sensorenabled or phoneuseenabled is given. 30 requests per minute per device (429). sensorenabled (optional) sets the opt-in. false turns the feature off: later events are not stored (counted as rejected) and existing ones are kept. Events are only stored while the opt-in is true, so the first upload should carry "sensorenabled": true. phoneuseenabled (optional) sets the separate phone-use opt-in. When omitted the stored value is kept. phoneuse events are accepted only while it is true (otherwise they count as rejected). Turning sensorenabled off also forces phone use off, even if phoneuseenabled: true is sent in the same request; turning the sensor back on does not bring it back. Response 200: {"accepted":n,"duplicate":n,"rejected":n,"sensorenabled":bool,"phoneuseenabled":bool}. Events are deduplicated on (user, kind, startedat), so retrying a request is safe. Invalid events are counted in rejected; the others are still stored. The audit log records counts only. Linking and merging A sensor event is attached to the trip whose [startedat, endedat] contains its start. If it arrives before the trip exists (or the trip is recomputed later) it stays unattached and is linked when the trip is stored. Unattached events still count in the report. Recomputing a trip (POST /trips/compute, the background job) replaces only source = 'gps' events; sensor events survive. Sensor wins. When a GPS-derived and a sensor event of the same user and kind overlap within +-4 s, only the sensor event is counted. GPS rows stay stored. The rule lives in one place, the SQL view tripeventseffective (migration 000101), which the report and the trip events query read. Report and trip changes GET /trips/report counts include sensor events. phoneuse is a number only for members with the sensor AND phone-use opt-in enabled and null for everyone else (a member without phone-use detection never reads 0); totals.events.phoneuse (and previoustotals) is the sum over those members, null if there are none. sensormembers: the user ids (of members the viewer can see) with the sensor enabled. phoneusemembers: the user ids with phone-use detection enabled. Compatibility. Clients up to v0.6.0 never send phoneuseenabled, so their stored value stays false: their phoneuse is null in reports and any phoneuse events they upload are now rejected (they used to be counted). Updating the app sends the flag from the phone-use switch. Every event of GET /trips/{id}/events (and GET /trips/{id}) has source (gps or sensor); lat / lon are null for sensor events without a fix. Accuracy limits These are estimates from phone GPS, not measurements, and not for enforcement. Sparse GPS under-counts. Phones often report a fix every 10-60 s to save battery. Acceleration is only computed between fixes at most 4 s apart, so a hard brake between two sparse fixes is invisible. Speeding is more robust. GPS speed is smoothed and noisy; occasional false events and missed events are expected. Tunnels, urban canyons and poor accuracy reduce quality. A passenger in a car is indistinguishable from a driver. Sensor events (below) are far more precise for braking and acceleration, but depend on the phone being in the car, mounted or not, and on the user having enabled the feature. Privacy Events carry a time and a location, so they are as sensitive as trips. A viewer sees a member's events (and counts in the report) only when they share a circle with that member AND the member shares their location in that circle. Outsiders and members with sharing off get 404 and are left out of the report; a member always sees their own events. Events are deleted with the user, included in GET /me/export (drivingevents, drivingsensorenabled, drivingphoneuseenabled) and pruned, including unattached sensor events, once older than LOCATIONRETENTIONDAYS. Sensor events are read through the same circle rules as trips. Crash detection (opt-in, default off) Settings > Driving detection > Detect possible crashes. Needs driving detection on. While a drive session is active the phone feeds accelerometer and GPS speed to CrashDetector (app/lib/services/driving/crashdetector.dart). A probable crash needs all of: acceleration magnitude >= 4 g, a GPS fix >= 25 km/h within 2.5 s before it, speed <= 2 m/s within 6 s after it, and speed staying <= 3 m/s for 3 s. Potholes, dropped phones and hard braking do not match. After a detection nothing more is reported for 5 minutes. Then a full-screen "Are you OK?" countdown (30 s, vibration and sound) runs: "I'm OK" cancels and nothing is sent; "I need help" sends at once and also posts /alerts/help; otherwise the alert goes out at 0. The background isolate sends POST /crash-alerts (device ingest key or Bearer token). The report is stored in crashevents (source = 'device', helprequested, peakg, columns added by EnsureCrashSchema) and pushed to circle members who can see the person's location, so it shows in Crash reports and the admin activity feed. The sender can mark it false alarm (POST /crashes/{id}/status). A device report suppresses a server-heuristic report for the same moment (+-2 min). Emergency services are never contacted. False-positive evidence (honest status) There is no field data yet. What exists: app/test/services/driving/crashdetectortest.dart replays synthetic traces that must NOT trigger (pothole at speed, phone dropped while driving/parked/walking/after stopping, hard braking without a spike, a spike with speed staying above the hold level, a slowdown only to 10 m/s, below 20 km/h, stale GPS, a spike just under 4 g) and traces that must (60 km/h spike then stop). Every false alarm is cheap: it only starts the cancelable 30 s "I'm OK" countdown and sends nothing unless it expires. Before treating the thresholds as proven, record real drives with detection on and count countdowns per 100 hours driven.

docs.title: On-device driving events (motion sensors)
docs.summary: Part of issue #45. GPS-only braking detection (server side) under-counts because a 1-60 s GPS cadence smooths a 1-2 s stop. When the user opts in, the Android app also uses the phone's accelerometer…

headings.text: Field-test checklist (nothing here was run on a device)

docs.text: On-device driving events (motion sensors) Part of issue #45. GPS-only braking detection (server side) under-counts because a 1-60 s GPS cadence smooths a 1-2 s stop. When the user opts in, the Android app also uses the phone's accelerometer and gyroscope while driving, detects hard braking and rapid acceleration on the device and uploads only the detected events. Privacy contract On by default, switch-off in Settings > Driving detection. A missing local preference (drivingsensorenabled) counts as ON, for new installs and for installs that update. The first time the app can (opening the Driving tab, or the next background location fix) it sends POST /trips/sensor-events with sensorenabled=true, then persists the effective value and a drivingsensorserversynced flag. A failed call leaves the flag unset and is retried (foreground and, at most every 10 minutes, the background service) until the server acknowledges it. The Driving tab shows a one-time, dismissible card ("Driving detection is on": motion sensor only while driving, only detected events uploaded, a button to Settings). "Seen" is local (drivingdetectiondisclosureseen). The "needs Driving detection" prompt on the page appears only when the user has turned detection off. Turning it off stops sampling at once (the runtime re-checks the switch every 5 s and on every fix), deletes the unsent queue and tells the server (sensorenabled=false); if that call fails it is redelivered like the opt-in. Existing uploaded events are kept. Raw samples live in memory inside the detector (a 30 s ring buffer) and are never written to disk or sent. Uploaded: kind, start/end time, magnitude and the latest GPS position. Sensors run only inside a driving session (below). Pipeline (app/lib/services/driving/) File Role motiondetector.dart Pure Dart detector (all maths, unit tested) drivingconfig.dart Thresholds, default 3.5 m/s^2, 400 ms, speed gate 5 m/s drivingsession.dart GPS-speed state machine that gates the sensors drivingruntime.dart Glue: session -> feed -> detector -> outbox -> upload drivingplatformfeed.dart sensorsplus + drivingnative plugin drivingeventoutbox.dart, drivingeventsservice.dart Queue, retry, batches phoneusetracker.dart Screen activity while moving (estimate) drivingbackground.dart Hook called from the background isolate Detector steps: gravity estimate (low-pass, rotated with the gyroscope so real braking does not leak into "gravity"), linear acceleration, projection onto the horizontal plane, forward axis learned from the car itself (during GPS speed changes >= 0.8 m/s^2 the mean horizontal acceleration is voted along the sign of the speed change; the sum points forward; needs >= 3 votes and 0.7 coherence; dropped if the phone tilts > 25 degrees or is handled), signed forward acceleration smoothed (150 ms), hysteresis episodes (>= threshold for >= 400 ms, exit at 80 %, 150 ms gap tolerance), cross-check with the GPS speed change over the event (sign and >= 40 % of the expected delta) and the speed gate (> 5 m/s before or after), merge of same-kind events < 2 s apart. When the axis becomes known the buffered history is replayed so the launch that taught the axis is still evaluated. Ignored: potholes (short, mostly vertical), gyro spikes 1.5 rad/s, horizontal acceleration > 12 m/s^2, any deviation from the gravity estimate > 8 m/s^2 (phone moved), episodes touching a handling event. Session / battery The existing background location service delivers a fix about every 60 s. A fix with speed >= 5 m/s arms a session: sensorsplus accelerometer and gyroscope at 50 Hz, and a 1 Hz GPS stream (platform LocationManager, no Play Services). The session is confirmed when speed stays >= 5 m/s for 10 s (else it stops after 90 s) and ends after 120 s below 5 m/s; every subscription is cancelled then, which unregisters the native listeners. Nothing samples while parked or walking. Consequence of the 60 s cadence: the first up to ~60 s of a trip are not covered (the first launch is usually missed). Android requirements No new permission. Accelerometer/gyroscope are not protected; 50 Hz is below the 200 Hz HIGHSAMPLINGRATESENSORS limit; ACTIVITYRECOGNITION is not needed for raw sensors (the existing entry is for the separate Play Services motion profile); the screen broadcasts need none; location is the existing background-location grant. Sensor events reach the app in the background only because the location foreground service (IsolateHolderService, type location) keeps the process alive. Without "Allow all the time" the service does not start and neither does detection. Plugin registration in the headless engine: the vendored locator creates FlutterEngine(context), whose constructor auto-registers GeneratedPluginRegistrant, so sensorsplus and drivingnative are available in the background isolate the same way batteryplus and secure storage already are. sensorsplus 7.1.1 registers a plain SensorManager listener without a max-report-latency, so hardware FIFO batching is not used. Acceptable because it only runs while driving; a native batched listener is a possible later optimisation. Phone use (phoneuse), Android, estimate only Implemented, default OFF and not changed by the detection default (second switch, requires the first). The app sends it to the server as phoneuseenabled with every opt-in sync; until it is true the server rejects phoneuse events and the report shows phone use as Off. The local plugin app/packages/drivingnative registers a receiver for ACTIONSCREENON, ACTIONSCREENOFF and ACTIONUSERPRESENT dynamically (they cannot be manifest-declared) on the application context, only while a driving session is running. Because it is registered in the headless engine hosted by the foreground service, the process and receiver live as long as tracking does. Detection (phoneusetracker.dart, handlinganalyzer.dart, thresholds in PhoneUseConfig, drivingconfig.dart) only counts time while GPS speed says the car is really moving (start >= 7 m/s, speed < 2 m/s is never counted, a stop of 6 s or more ends the event, the first and last 10 s of a drive are ignored). Evidence: Screen + handling. The accelerometer/gyroscope are already sampled while driving; a pure HandlingAnalyzer reduces them to one verdict per 2 s window (rotation about non-vertical axes, corroborated accelerometer deviation). It only runs while the screen is lit or a call is active. An unlocked, handled phone counts, also when it was already lit before the drive (no unlock event). A tap on an unlock counts 12 s; a lit screen that is not being handled is a mounted navigation display and is not counted; proximity "near" without handling (pocket/bag) is ignored. With no motion data at all it falls back to the unlocked screen. Calls. The plugin's context channel reports proximity, call mode (AudioManager.mode), the call audio route and Android car UI mode, with no permission (no READPHONESTATE, no BLUETOOTHCONNECT). A handset call at the ear counts; a speakerphone call only while handled; Bluetooth, wired headset, Android Auto/car routes are hands-free and are NOT counted. If the route cannot be determined, a call is counted only with proximity "near". Interactions < 10 s apart merge; magnitude is the seconds of actual interaction, an event spans at most 180 s and at most 8 events per drive are kept. Optional fields maxspeedmps, confidence (0..1) and activity (screen / call) are sent; the server stores them (migration 000122). The owner can dismiss one phone-use event (PATCH /trips/events/{id}) or mark a drive as passenger (PUT /trips/{id}/passenger); both leave every report, score and weekly summary (view tripeventseffective). Nobody else can. All thresholds are educated guesses, not calibrated on real vehicles. It cannot tell a passenger from a driver (hence the passenger/dismiss actions), cannot tell Android Auto reliably on every phone, and never sees apps or content. No UsageStats or accessibility permission. Not covered / known limits Android only; iOS has no equivalent here. Forward axis needs one clear acceleration or braking (about 3 s) after start or after the phone is moved; events before that are replayed from the buffer, but a phone repositioned mid-event may lose it. Pothole/handling rejection thresholds are conservative guesses that must be tuned with real drives. Field-test checklist (nothing here was run on a device) 1. Sensor rate in the background isolate (screen off, app swiped away): log the achieved Hz of accelerometer/gyro and GPS in a debug build. 2. Detection accuracy in a real car with phone in cup holder, mount, pocket, seat; compare against a reference (OBD or a second app). 3. False positives: potholes, speed bumps, pickup, dropping, passenger handling. 4. Battery drain on a one-hour drive and on a parked day (should be zero extra). 5. Screen events under Doze/app standby, and after the OS kills the process. 6. Devices without gyroscope; GPS Doppler speed absent; OEM background limits. 7. Opt-out: switch off mid-drive stops sampling within ~5 s and the server receives sensorenabled=false.

docs.title: Push notifications
docs.summary: Orbitly can deliver alerts (SOS, help, check-in, geofence arrivals) and silent commands (location refresh requests) over three transports. A phone never needs Google services, and on Android it no…

headings.text: What happens when Android kills or freezes the process

docs.text: Push notifications Orbitly can deliver alerts (SOS, help, check-in, geofence arrivals) and silent commands (location refresh requests) over three transports. A phone never needs Google services, and on Android it no longer needs a second app. Transport Platform Needs Reaches a phone that is... Direct (built in) Android nothing; on by default connected to your server (see limits below) UnifiedPush / ntfy Android the ntfy app (or another distributor) and an ntfy server dozing or with the app stopped, as long as the distributor is alive APNs iOS an Apple developer account and a .p8 key anywhere Apple can reach The transports are independent. A device can use direct and UnifiedPush at the same time; the server picks per device (below). ntfy/UnifiedPush stays supported and is now optional. Direct channel How it works 1. On sign-in the app registers the device with pushtransport: "direct" (PATCH /devices/{id}), and makes sure it holds a device ingest key. 2. While it is allowed to run, the app keeps one authenticated HTTPS connection open: GET /push/stream (Server-Sent Events), authenticated with X-Device-Key: <deviceid>.<ingestkey>, the same credential the background location reporter uses. A bearer token plus ?deviceid= also works. 3. When an alert is created the server writes an event into the device's pushoutbox row set and, if the device is connected, wakes its stream. The app shows a local notification and acknowledges the event with POST /push/ack. 4. A device that is offline keeps its events (bounded, with a TTL) and receives them the next time it connects. Frames on the stream: event: hello (once), event: push (data is the payload), : hb comment heartbeats every 55 seconds, and event: bye with a reason (revoked, closed or replaced) before the server closes. Delivery guarantees At least once. An event stays queued until the device acknowledges it and is re-sent on every reconnect. The app deduplicates on the event id and derives the notification id from it, so a re-send replaces rather than stacks. Queue limits. Latest 50 undelivered events per device. TTLs: alerts 6 h, geofence notices 1 h, commands 5 min. Expired alert events are recorded as a failed delivery (expired) in the alert's delivery list. Delivery state (alertdeliveries, channel push): queued when stored, sent when written to the device's open stream, delivered when the device acknowledged it, acknowledged when the person confirmed the alert in the app (POST /alerts/{id}/ack, which also retires that alert's queued events on the user's other devices). delivered means the phone has the notification, not that someone read it. Transport choice per device. A direct device always gets the event queued. If it is not connected right now and also registered a UnifiedPush endpoint, the server additionally sends through UnifiedPush. A connected device gets direct only. Devices without direct behave exactly as before. Privacy Payloads are built from the same title and body the UnifiedPush and APNs senders use, so they never contain coordinates and carry no sender name or note unless VERBOSEPUSH=true. They only add the alert id (to open the right screen) and a dedupe id. Events travel from your server to your phone only; no third party sees them. The stream is plain TLS to your own origin. A test scans direct payloads for coordinates and names. Authentication, limits and revocation Auth failures return 401. A device only streams for itself; a bearer token for another user's device gets 404. At most 8 simultaneous device streams per user; more get 429. A second stream for the same device replaces the first (the old one receives bye: replaced). Connect attempts are rate limited per user. The server rechecks credentials every 20 seconds while a stream is open and closes it (bye: revoked) after logout, password change, ingest-key rotation or expiry, access-token expiry (bearer streams), and device deletion. Logout and device deletion also close it immediately. Behind Caddy the stream path is excluded from gzip and buffering (see caddy/Caddyfile). Other reverse proxies must disable response buffering for /push/stream and allow idle connections for a few minutes. Setup Nothing, on a default install. DIRECTPUSH=false in .env disables it (GET /config then reports directpush: false and apps skip registration). Family members only need background location permission and, recommended, the battery-optimization exemption that onboarding already asks for. Battery The app holds a single TCP connection and the server sends one tiny heartbeat every 55 seconds, so the radio wakes about once a minute while the connection is up. The app treats 150 seconds of silence as a dead connection and reconnects with exponential backoff (2 s doubling to 5 min, with jitter); a network change (Wi-Fi to mobile, coming back online) reconnects at once. The connection is held by the background location foreground service (its isolate keeps it alive and revives it on every location fix and heartbeat), so no extra service or notification is added. Location reporting already keeps the device awake for fixes, which makes the marginal cost small but not zero. The foreground UI holds a connection only while the app is open and the location service is not running. If background location is not granted ("Allow all the time"), there is no foreground service and the connection exists only while the app is open. What happens when Android kills or freezes the process The direct channel needs a live process. Honest limits: Process killed (swipe-away on some vendors, memory pressure, force stop): nothing can receive until the process runs again. Queued events then arrive the next time the location service or the app starts, within their TTL. An SOS is not lost, but it can be late. Doze and OEM battery savers can freeze the network for a foreground service on deeply idle devices. This is weaker than FCM, which uses a system-level connection that survives those states. Recommended mitigation: accept the battery-optimization exemption during setup (or set the app to "Unrestricted"/"Don't optimize"), and keep background location on. If that is not enough for a family member's phone, additionally install ntfy: with both configured, a disconnected phone is also reached through ntfy. UnifiedPush / ntfy (optional) Unchanged: the device registers its distributor endpoint (unifiedpushendpoint) and the server POSTs the message to it. Set NTFYBASEURL (and PUSHADDRESS/the push compose profile for the bundled ntfy server, see docs/self-hosting.md). The server validates endpoints to https and public addresses only. Use it for phones where the direct channel is too fragile, or when you already run ntfy. APNs (iOS) Set APNSKEYFILE, APNSKEYID, APNSTEAMID and APNSTOPIC. Alerts are sent as visible pushes and location refreshes as silent content-available pushes. The direct channel is Android only. API summary Method Path Auth Purpose GET /push/stream device key or bearer + deviceid event stream POST /push/ack same {"deviceid","ids":[...]}, up to 50, marks delivered PATCH /devices/{id} bearer pushtransport: "direct" or "" POST /devices bearer accepts pushtransport at registration Verification status Server code is covered by table-driven and real-Postgres tests (queueing, ack, dedupe, TTL, bounded queue, connection cap, auth failure, close on revocation, payload contents). The Android client has unit tests with fakes (SSE parsing, backoff, routing, reconnect logic). It has not been run on a physical device: foreground-service behaviour, Doze behaviour and notification tap routing from the background isolate still need on-device testing. Per-member notification settings Each user can choose which alerts they get about each other member they share a circle with: arrivals, departures, low battery, driving/speeding, mute-all, and optional quiet hours (GET/PUT/DELETE /members/{id}/notification-prefs, table notificationprefs). A user can only read and edit their own settings, and only about members of circles they share (anything else is 404). Geofence arrival/departure pushes honour the settings when the event's device rows are created. A lookup error fails open (the push is sent). SOS, help and check-in alerts are never filtered, whatever the settings say: the filter only recognises the four optional categories. Low-battery and driving/speeding settings are stored and enforced by the same filter (notifSuppressed), but the server does not yet send push notifications for those events, so nothing consumes them today. Quiet hours use the phone's UTC offset (UTC+05:30) or an IANA zone; a fixed offset does not follow daylight saving until the app re-saves.

docs.title: SMS providers
docs.summary: SMS is optional. With no provider configured the app works fully: alerts go in-app (WebSocket and push) and nothing is sent by SMS. Phone numbers are optional on every account.
docs.text: SMS providers SMS is optional. With no provider configured the app works fully: alerts go in-app (WebSocket and push) and nothing is sent by SMS. Phone numbers are optional on every account. Pick a provider with SMSPROVIDER (default twilio, so existing TWILIO deployments are unchanged). Credentials use the same three variables for every provider (SMSACCOUNTID, SMSAUTHTOKEN, SMSFROM are provider-neutral aliases of TWILIOACCOUNTSID, TWILIOAUTHTOKEN, TWILIOFROM): Provider SMSPROVIDER ACCOUNTID AUTHTOKEN FROM Extra Twilio twilio Account SID Auth token sender number Telnyx telnyx unused API key (v2) sender number Plivo plivo Auth ID Auth token source number / sender id Amazon SNS sns access key id secret access key optional sender id SMSREGION (e.g. us-east-1) The admin Settings screen edits the credential fields; provider and region come from the environment. Unknown providers or missing credentials disable SMS. Code: backend/internal/sms (Dispatcher interface, providers.go, tests with fake HTTP servers in providerstest.go). Abuse limits Emergency contacts must be verified-by-opt-in in practice: SMS fan-out is capped per sender per day, per recipient and per family per hour (ALERTSMS, see docs/safety.md), and check-ins do not SMS by default. A2P / compliance notes US 10DLC and toll-free numbers require carrier registration (A2P) before messages are reliably delivered; unregistered traffic is filtered. Register the brand and campaign with your provider. Messages are transactional safety alerts to people a family member named as a contact. Honour STOP/HELP keywords (providers do this on the sender number). Messages never contain coordinates; they link to an expiring share page and never claim that emergency services were called. Amazon SNS needs a sandbox exit and an origination identity in many regions.

docs.title: Passkeys (WebAuthn) sign-in
docs.summary: Server side is implemented with github.com/go-webauthn/webauthn (backend/internal/handlers/passkeys.go). The Flutter client and web admin ceremonies are not built yet (see "Status").
docs.text: Passkeys (WebAuthn) sign-in Server side is implemented with github.com/go-webauthn/webauthn (backend/internal/handlers/passkeys.go). The Flutter client and web admin ceremonies are not built yet (see "Status"). Enabling Passkeys are off unless the server knows its public origin. Set PUBLICBASEURL=https://family.example.com (the relying party id and origin are derived from it) or set explicitly WEBAUTHNRPID and WEBAUTHNORIGINS (comma separated). Plain http origins do not enable passkeys. Android app origins (android:apk-key-hash:...) need a Digital Asset Links file on the host and are not configured yet. API Endpoint Auth Purpose POST /auth/passkeys/register/begin {password, totpcode?} bearer Step-up (password, plus TOTP when on) then returns {challengeid, options} for navigator.credentials.create / Credential Manager. POST /auth/passkeys/register/finish?challengeid=&name= body = credential JSON bearer Verifies attestation, stores the credential. 201 {id, name}. POST /auth/passkeys/login/begin none Usernameless (discoverable) sign-in options. POST /auth/passkeys/login/finish?challengeid= body = assertion JSON none Returns the normal token pair. GET /auth/passkeys bearer Lists id, name, created, last used (no key material). DELETE /auth/passkeys/{id} bearer Removes one of your passkeys. Security decisions Enrolling needs the password (and TOTP): a stolen access token cannot add a passkey. User verification is required, so a passkey login is itself two-factor and does not prompt for TOTP. Challenges are stored server side (passkeychallenges), single use, valid 5 minutes. Login/finish is rate limited like password login. The claimed user handle must own the credential; a sign counter that does not increase (cloned authenticator) is refused and audited. Attestation is not requested ("none"); we need possession, not device provenance. Recovery is unchanged: the password and admin/family reset codes keep working, and any passkey can be removed from a signed-in session. Max 10 per account. Credentials are deleted with the account (ON DELETE CASCADE). Status Tests: backend/internal/handlers/passkeystest.go run full register and login ceremonies with a software authenticator (ES256, none attestation) against Postgres, including wrong origin, replayed/expired challenge, forged signature, foreign user handle, counter regression, cross-user finish and deletion. Not done: the Android client (Credential Manager needs a vetted Flutter plugin and an assetlinks.json for the host), iOS (needs an Apple account and associated domains) and the web-admin UI. Those are required for the issue's "enroll and login on both platforms" criterion.
