headings.text: Decision: the phone is the only holder of secrets
Standalone LTE mode (future work, not built)

docs.text: Watch apps (companion model) The phone holds all secrets and sends watches a small readable snapshot; watches send back a fixed set of commands. Status: Wear OS part implemented in v0.25 (unreleased). The Apple Watch part is written by the Apple Watch workstream and is kept in its own section at the end; the snapshot and command contract below is shared so both watches speak the same language to the phone. Decision: the phone is the only holder of secrets Orbitly's watches are companions. The phone app stays the only place that holds the sign-in token, the Private-circle (end-to-end) keys and the server address. It pushes a small, already-readable snapshot to the watch. The watch sends commands back ("I'm OK", SOS, pause sharing). The phone runs them with its own credentials and keys. Why: Private circles keep working. Positions in a Private circle can only be decrypted on a phone that holds the circle key. A watch that talked to the server directly would need that key too (a new device to approve, a new key wrap, a new thing to lose). With the companion model no key or token ever exists on the watch. No new server surface. The server, API and migrations do not change. The watch is not a "device" in the server's eyes. Battery. The watch does no networking and no polling. It wakes only when the phone changes the snapshot. Trade-off (said plainly in the user docs): the watch is only as live as its phone. If the phone is off, out of Bluetooth/Wi-Fi range, or Orbitly is not running on it, the watch shows the last snapshot with its age and a "phone not connected" note, and commands cannot be delivered. A watch with its own LTE cannot work alone (see "Standalone LTE mode" below). server <--TLS--> PHONE (tokens, E2EE keys, decrypts) <--Bluetooth/Wi-Fi--> WATCH snapshot (JSON, < 100 KB) ---------------------> (no secrets) <------------------------- command (small JSON) Security Pairing is the trust boundary. On Wear OS the Wearable Data Layer only delivers data between a phone and the watch it is paired to, and only between apps with the same applicationId signed with the same key. The watch app uses app.openfamily (like the phone app) and the same release signing key (CI uses the same keystore secrets). A different app, or a differently signed build, cannot read the snapshot or send commands. The watch trusts only its paired phone. The watch app never opens a network connection and does not request INTERNET. Commands are a fixed vocabulary. The phone accepts only the commands listed below, with size limits, a replay window and per-command rate limits. Chat quick replies are sent as an id ("omw"); the phone maps the id to the text, so the watch cannot make the phone send arbitrary text. SOS from the watch needs a deliberate press-and-hold plus a 5 second countdown with cancel. The phone additionally refuses a second SOS within 60 s. Orbitly never contacts emergency services; the watch says so. What leaves the phone. The snapshot contains names, last positions (lat/lon), place names, addresses, battery, and alert text for the circle the phone currently shows. For a Private circle that is plaintext on the phone-watch link and on the watch's storage, but it never goes to the server or any third party by Orbitly. On Wear OS the Data Layer transfer goes over the local Bluetooth/Wi-Fi link between the paired devices; Google Play services on the phone and the watch handle it (Google's servers are not used for the transfer, but the Data Layer is a Google component, which is the accepted trade-off). Users who do not want plaintext of a Private circle on a watch can turn the watch bridge off in Settings, Watch (Private circles can also be excluded: "Show Private circles on the watch", default on, off removes them from the snapshot). Sign-out on the phone, or turning the bridge off, deletes the Data Layer item and is a debt, not a best effort: a persistent clear-pending flag (in Dart preferences and in native preferences) is set first. The clear counts as paid only when the delete succeeded and a watch was connected to receive it. Otherwise the flag stays, no snapshot is published (Dart refuses, and the native publish refuses) until the user signs in again, and the debt is paid the next time a watch connects (the watch app's orbitlywatchapp capability appears: WatchListenerService.onCapabilityChanged, which also works with the app closed, and a runtime CapabilityClient listener while it runs) or at the next app start. Just before sending, the bridge re-checks enabled, signed in and not-pending, so a snapshot being built during a sign-out cannot override the clear. On the watch, a deleted item, an empty (signedIn: false) snapshot, or a connected phone with no snapshot item at all wipes the stored snapshot and redraws the tile and complication empty. Dim/ambient: the watch app shows names and places in ambient mode, same as the Wear OS system does for other apps; no extra privacy layer is added. Snapshot (phone to watch) One JSON document, UTF-8, v: 1. Hard cap 100 KB (the phone drops the least important members until it fits; in practice it is about 3 to 6 KB for a family). { "v": 1, "ts": 1767225600000, "signedIn": true, "scope": {"id": "all", "name": "Everyone", "private": false}, "circles": [{"id": "c1", "name": "Family", "unread": 2, "private": false}], "me": {"sharing": "on", "pausedUntil": null}, "unread": 2, "members": [{ "id": "u1", "name": "Sam", "initials": "S", "color": 4283215696, "lat": 51.5, "lon": -0.12, "fixAt": 1767225500000, "battery": 63, "state": "driving", "speedKmh": 68, "place": "Home", "address": "12 High St", "line": "Driving 40 mph", "private": false, "you": false }, { "id": "u2", "name": "Ana", "state": "still", "line": "Left Work", "lineAt": 1767224100000, "...": "..." }], "alerts": [{"id": "a1", "kind": "sos", "from": "Sam", "at": 1767225000000, "note": "", "active": true}], "lastCommand": {"id": "k9", "cmd": "checkin", "ok": true, "at": 1767225590000, "message": ""} } state is one of driving, moving, atplace, still, stopped, none. line is the phone's own one-line status text, so the watch and the phone always say the same thing (units follow the phone's setting), minus anything that changes by itself as time passes: the driving speed is rounded to 5 mph, and a relative time is split off into lineAt (epoch ms). The watch shows line + " " + age(lineAt) ("Left Work 25 min ago", "Updates stopped, last seen 3 d ago"), counting the age on its own clock. A watch app that does not know lineAt shows the line alone. Ages are worded just now, N min ago, N h ago, N d ago on both watches (shared vectors in the Kotlin and Dart tests). ts is when the snapshot was built; the watch shows "updated N min ago" from it. Members carry their own fixAt (when the position was taken). lastCommand is how the phone answers a command; a watch matches id with the command it sent. This avoids a second channel and is delta-friendly. The Apple Watch uses the same JSON (WatchConnectivity applicationContext). Positions are rounded to 5 decimals (about 1 m). Members are capped at 15. Cadence Every snapshot wakes the watch, rewrites its stored copy and may redraw the tile and complication, so the phone sends only what the watch needs, at the pace the watch asked for. All of it lives in the shared Dart bridge (watchsnapshot.dart, watchbridge.dart), so Wear OS and the Apple Watch behave the same. Nothing in the snapshot ticks by itself. The content hash is the snapshot without ts, and nothing else in it changes as time passes: ages are formatted on the watch from fixAt, lineAt and the alert at. A minute passing never produces a snapshot. What changed decides how soon it goes out (classifyWatchChange, compared with the last snapshot the watch actually got): Change Examples Sent Urgent urgent an alert arrived or ended; the answer to a watch command; first snapshot after sign-in, app start or a watch (re)connecting within the 5 s floor yes event unread count, sharing paused or resumed within the 5 s floor only if the watch app is on screen meaningful someone moved more than 100 m from where the watch last saw them, changed state (driving, at a place, stopped), place, status text or battery step (5% at 20% and below, 10% above), joined or left; circles or scope changed at the tier's pace (below) only if the watch app is on screen minor GPS jitter under 100 m, a newer fix time, a driving speed step with the next keep-alive, or within 5 s while the app is on screen as the tier none identical apart from ts never Tiers: the watch says whether it is on screen. The watch app sends visible when it comes on screen and every 60 s while it stays there, visible with arg ambient when it goes into always-on mode, and hidden when it leaves. A visible not repeated within 150 s (an ambient within 15 min) expires by itself, so a lost hidden costs nothing. Tier Meaningful changes Keep-alive Data Layer visible every change, at most one snapshot per 5 s; a fresh one right away when the app comes on screen 60 s (keeps "Updated" current) urgent ambient at most once per 60 s 10 min urgent hidden (default) at most once per 2 min 10 min not urgent: the system may batch it for a few minutes The roster is looked at no more than once per 5 s whatever the tier. Pushed changes (alerts, unread, sharing) skip that floor. Measured in app/test/services/watch/watchcadencetest.dart (one simulated hour, deterministic data; before = the same hour through the previous logic; the two urgent ones in the quiet hours are the start-up snapshot and the first roster after it): Hour Before After (hidden) Urgent after one person driving at 1 Hz 720, all urgent 31 2 still family with GPS jitter 125, all urgent 7 2 still family plus 4 alerts, 20 chat messages, a pause 125, all urgent 31 7 one person driving, watch app on screen 720 721 all one person driving, watch app in always-on 720 61 all No polling for the watch. Alerts and the pause state used to be fetched over REST every minute while a watch was connected (about 126 requests an hour). They are now fetched once and again only when the live socket reports an alert or acknowledgement, the socket reconnects, or this phone pauses or resumes, with a 10-minute safety refresh: 18 requests an hour. Link state. The Wear app advertises the capability orbitlywatchapp (wear/app/src/main/res/values/wear.xml). The phone listens for it with a CapabilityClient listener while the app runs and through WatchListenerService (manifest CAPABILITYCHANGED, path /orbitlywatchapp) while it does not; status counts reachable nodes with the capability. A watch running an older Orbitly app does not advertise it: then any connected watch counts as before, and its comings and goings are only noticed by the 10-minute keep-alive re-check (the old peer callbacks needed the deprecated BINDLISTENER, which Android lint rejects). Not verified on a device: whether CAPABILITYCHANGED is delivered to the closed app on every Wear OS and Play services version. On the watch (Wear OS). An identical item is dropped with one string comparison. The tile and complication are redrawn only when what they show changed (SurfaceGate): signed in, unread, sharing or who has a position at once; positions (about 100 m) and fix times (to the minute) at most once a minute; battery, status text, alerts and keep-alives never. When the app leaves the screen they are redrawn once with the latest data. Commands (watch to phone) Wear OS: MessageClient, path /orbitly/cmd, payload a small JSON: {"id": "<random>", "cmd": "<name>", "at": <ms>, "arg": "<optional>"}. cmd arg What the phone does sos none Sends the same SOS as the in-app button (POST /alerts/sos with its own location, sealed position for Private circles). checkin none "I'm OK" check-in to the circle (POST /alerts/check-in). pause minutes (15, 60, 240) Pauses sharing for that time. resume none Resumes sharing. ack alert id Marks an alert seen (POST /alerts/{id}/ack). refresh none Rebuilds and publishes the snapshot now (still rate limited to once per 5 s). reply reply id (ok, omw, late, call, thanks) Sends the fixed text to the circle chat the phone has open (or the first circle). visible none, or ambient The watch app is on screen (or in always-on mode): faster cadence (see Cadence). Never answered in lastCommand. hidden none The watch app left the screen: back to the slow cadence. Never answered. The phone replies through lastCommand in the next snapshot. A command is valid for 2 minutes after at (replay window; the watch and phone clocks only need to agree to within that) and an id is processed once. When the phone app is not running. Commands are handled by the Orbitly app process. If the Flutter engine is not running the native receiver answers the watch straight away with ok: false ("Open Orbitly on your phone") instead of queueing: a stale SOS that fires minutes later would be worse than a clear failure. The watch therefore always tells the user whether the command arrived, and the SOS screen says "If it did not send, call emergency services". Wear OS app Separate Gradle project in wear/ (Kotlin, Jetpack Compose for Wear OS, androidx.wear.compose Material), minSdk 30 (Wear OS 3+: Galaxy Watch 4 and newer, Pixel Watch, Fossil Gen 6, TicWatch Pro 5 and others). Older Tizen Galaxy Watches (Watch 3 and earlier, Active, Gear) are not supported: they are a different operating system. applicationId app.openfamily, versionName/versionCode computed from the release tag exactly as for the phone APK (wear.yml and apk.yml share the formula; locally the version is read from app/pubspec.yaml). The watch versionCode gets +1 added to the phone's code only if Play requires distinct codes for the two form factors, which it does not for separate apps in one listing. com.google.android.wearable.standalone is false: the app needs the phone for all its data. Play then lists it as a companion-dependent watch app. Setting it to true would claim the watch works alone, which is not true in this design. Updates arrive by DataClient changes only (a WearableListenerService is woken by the system; the UI collects from a StateFlow). No polling, no background service, no wake locks. The only repeating message is visible once a minute while the app is on screen and not in ambient mode. Screens: People, Person (place, age, "Open on phone", distance and direction), SOS (hold to arm, 5 s countdown, cancel, haptics), I'm OK, Sharing pause and resume, Quick replies with unread badge, Alerts. A Tile ("Circle", the people nearest to you) and a Complication (nearest member, unread, sharing state). Distance and direction use the watch's last known location (only if the user grants location permission on the watch) and the member's coordinates; there is no map. Offline: the last snapshot is stored on the watch (DataClient item or a copy in app storage) and shown with its age; the header shows "Phone not connected". headings.text: Sign-out and switch-off are a debt
What the first CI run must prove

docs.text: Apple Watch app (companion model) Status: written without a Mac. No Swift, Xcode project change, plist or workflow in this feature has been compiled, run in a simulator or tried on a watch. The shared Dart side is tested on Linux (watchbridgetest.dart). Read What the first CI run must prove before trusting any line here. This page is the Apple half of WATCHAPPS.md, which owns the decision, the security model, the snapshot JSON and the command table for both watches. This page only covers what is specific to Apple. Pieces Piece File Role Watch app (SwiftUI, watchOS 9+) app/ios/OrbitlyWatch/.swift UI, last snapshot in UserDefaults iPhone native bridge app/ios/Runner/WatchBridge.swift WCSession delegate, channel app.openfamily/watch Dart bridge (shared with Wear OS) app/lib/services/watch/watchbridge.dart throttle, commands, sign-out debt Snapshot model (shared) app/lib/services/watch/watchsnapshot.dart JSON contract, single source of truth Settings screen (shared) app/lib/screens/watchsettingsscreen.dart one "Watch" row, wording follows the platform Xcode target app/ios/Runner.xcodeproj (ids AB1C0DE0...) target OrbitlyWatch, embedded in the iPhone app Kill switch scripts/ios-watch-target.py removes the target from the project Transport (WatchConnectivity) Direction API Used for phone to watch updateApplicationContext(["snapshot": json, "session": id]) the latest snapshot; newer replaces older, no queue phone to watch updateApplicationContext(["cleared": true, "session": id?]) sign-out or switch off: the watch deletes its copy watch to phone sendMessage(["json": command], replyHandler) every command; needs the phone reachable. The reply only means "taken"; the result is lastCommand in the next snapshot No polling on either side. The watch waits at most 20 seconds for the phone's answer and then says "No confirmation from the iPhone". Nothing is queued, so a stale SOS can never fire later. Cadence (same Dart bridge as Wear OS, WATCHAPPS.md, Cadence): the watch app sends visible when its scene becomes active and once a minute while it stays active (the only timer, and only while on screen), visible with ambient when the scene goes inactive (wrist down, always-on), and hidden in the background, all fire and forget through sendMessage when the iPhone is reachable. The iPhone then sends every few seconds while the app is on screen and only meaningful changes, at most every 2 minutes, otherwise. updateApplicationContext has no urgency switch, so the urgent flag the bridge passes is ignored on the iPhone. Member lines with a relative time come as line plus lineAt, and the watch adds the age itself ("Left Work 25 min ago"). The Swift changes for this were not compiled here (no Xcode on the build host); the first macOS CI run proves them. Sign-out and switch-off are a debt The shared Dart bridge keeps its pending flag. The native side adds two persisted facts of its own: blocked (no data may be sent: set by clear, lifted by allowPublish) and clearUndelivered (the wipe has not yet been accepted by WatchConnectivity). A new sign-in does not reset clearUndelivered: allowPublish creates a new session id and sends the wipe first (and with the new id). Every context carries the session id; the watch drops what it stored for any other session, a cleared context, or a snapshot with signedIn: false. clear answers true to Dart only once the wipe was handed over. Known gap on the Wear OS side (not changed here): its allowPublish clears the native pending flag without first making sure an undelivered delete reached the watch. A new snapshot replaces the item, so the old data is overwritten once the watch is reachable, but until then the watch can still show the old user's data. The same session-id idea would close it. Watch UI People list (initials avatar, name, "At Home" / "Driving 42 mph" / "2 min ago", battery), person detail (place, address, age, battery, Handoff note), Distance and direction (north-up arrow, see below), SOS, I'm OK, Pause or Resume sharing, Quick replies with an unread badge, Alerts. Dynamic Type is respected (system text styles, line limits of 1 to 2 lines, scrolling views). Offline: the last snapshot is shown with "iPhone not reachable" and its age. Direction view limitation: the arrow is north-up, computed by the phone. It does not turn with your wrist (no heading sensor is read, to keep the battery). A live heading is future work. Complications: not shipped A WidgetKit complication needs a widget extension target, an App Group (or shared Keychain) to read the snapshot, and a second set of pbxproj objects. With nothing able to compile here that doubles the chance of breaking the iPhone build, so v1 ships without complications. Future: a widget extension inside the watch app reading the snapshot from an App Group group.app.openfamily (accessoryCircular: unread or battery of the first person; accessoryRectangular: two people; accessoryInline: "Anna at Home"). Standalone LTE: future work only Evaluated, not built. It would need: a watch-side login (QR or code from the phone), tokens in the watch Keychain, the E2EE circle keys copied to the watch (or Private circles hidden there), a polling or push strategy for a device that sleeps (APNs to the watch), and its own SOS location (the watch GPS). Verdict: worth doing after the companion version has proven itself, and only with Private circles excluded on the watch unless the owner decides otherwise. Xcode project Hand-edited project.pbxproj (no XcodeGen: nothing could install and run it here, and a second tool in the release path is a second thing to break). All Watch objects use ids that start with AB1C0DE0, which is what makes the kill switch exact. Target OrbitlyWatch, product type application, SDKROOT=watchos, SUPPORTEDPLATFORMS="watchos watchsimulator", WATCHOSDEPLOYMENTTARGET=9.0, TARGETEDDEVICEFAMILY=4, bundle id app.openfamily.watchkitapp, SWIFTVERSION=5.0, Info.plist WKApplication=true, WKCompanionAppBundleIdentifier=app.openfamily. Runner gets a target dependency on it and an Embed Watch Content copy phase (destination Products Directory, path $(CONTENTSFOLDERPATH)/Watch), placed before "Thin Binary" to avoid a build cycle. The watch target has its own Watch.xcconfig that only includes Generated.xcconfig, to get FLUTTERBUILDNAME and FLUTTERBUILDNUMBER so the watch version equals the iPhone version (the App Store checks this). It deliberately does not use Flutter's Release.xcconfig, because the signed-release workflow appends the iPhone bundle id and provisioning profile to that file. Signing: CODESIGNSTYLE=Automatic with no team. Unsigned CI builds pass CODESIGNINGALLOWED=NO so no profile is needed. App icon: the 1024 px Orbitly icon as the single watchOS icon (copied from the iPhone asset, which assets/brand/build-rasters.mjs regenerates; copy it again when the brand changes). Accent color is the brand lime. Kill switch If the watch target breaks the iPhone build: python3 scripts/ios-watch-target.py disable git add app/ios && git commit -m "Remove the Apple Watch target from the Xcode project" It strips every AB1C0DE0 object from the pbxproj and deletes the OrbitlyWatch scheme. The result was verified byte for byte against the project without the watch (done in Docker on Linux). The iPhone side (WatchBridge.swift, the Dart bridge) stays and finds no watch. Check the project with python3 scripts/ios-watch-target.py check; re-enable with git revert. Builds and signing Simulator job (test.yml job ios) is unchanged and still blocking. It now builds the watch app as a dependency of Runner, so it is also the first thing to fail if the project edit is wrong. Watch job (test.yml job watchos) builds -scheme OrbitlyWatch for generic/platform=watchOS Simulator, builds the iPhone app and checks that Runner.app/Watch/OrbitlyWatch.app exists. continue-on-error: true for now. Unsigned IPA (ios-unsigned.yml): cp -R of Runner.app already carries Watch/; a new check fails the job if the project has the watch target but the app is missing, and the IPA listing is checked for it. Sideload tools must sign the watch bundle too (see the user page). Signed TestFlight (ios-release.yml): the watch app needs its own App Store profile and an entry in ExportOptions.plist. Until the owner sets repository variable IOSWATCHENABLED=true and adds those, the workflow runs the kill switch first, so the signed path behaves exactly as before. Needed for enabling: App ID app.openfamily.watchkitapp, an App Store profile, a second provisioningProfiles entry. What the first CI run must prove Nothing below has ever happened. 1. python3 scripts/ios-watch-target.py check passes on the runner (it does on Linux). 2. xcodebuild -showsdks lists a watchOS Simulator SDK on macos-15; if not, nothing here can build. 3. The SwiftUI and WatchConnectivity sources compile with the runner's Swift (the most likely failures are small type or API mistakes in OrbitlyWatch/.swift). 4. The asset catalog compiles (single 1024 px watchOS icon, accent color). 5. Xcode accepts the hand-written target: no "cycle in dependencies", no missing file, no "Info.plist" or "product" error. 6. The existing iPhone jobs still pass: flutter build ios --simulator and the RunnerTests job, with the watch app built as a dependency for the matching simulator SDK. Flutter passes -sdk iphonesimulator style arguments; whether Xcode then builds the watch dependency with the watch simulator SDK is unproven. 7. flutter build ios --release --no-codesign (unsigned IPA job) embeds Watch/OrbitlyWatch.app and the IPA zip contains it. 8. Runner/WatchBridge.swift compiles and the iPhone app still launches in the simulator (simctl launch). 9. Not provable in CI at all: pairing, install through the iPhone Watch app, the snapshot arriving, SOS and every command end to end, Handoff, layout on the small and large watch sizes, Dynamic Type. That needs a real iPhone and watch. Risk to the iPhone release The pbxproj edit touches the iPhone target (a dependency and an embed phase). If it is wrong, the whole iOS build fails, including the unsigned IPA. Mitigations: the new job is separate, the kill switch is one command and tested for exactness, the signed workflow disables the watch by default, and the Xcode edit follows the layout Xcode 14+ itself writes for a single-target watch app. Remaining risk: a build setting or phase ordering that only a real Xcode rejects. If the first CI run is red in the ios job after this merges, run the kill switch before anything else.

docs.title: Performance of Private (phone-only) circles
docs.summary: Scope: release 0.23.1 work on the lag reported on an Android phone while a circle runs in Private mode: a laggy bottom sheet, a slow UI, and members showing "location not available".

headings.text: What was found (by reading the code, then confirmed by the benchmarks)
"Location not available" in Private mode: the cause and the wording
On-device reports are an opt-in switch, off by default
Startup and release configuration (checked, no change needed)

docs.text: Performance of Private (phone-only) circles Scope: release 0.23.1 work on the lag reported on an Android phone while a circle runs in Private mode: a laggy bottom sheet, a slow UI, and members showing "location not available". Important: every number below was measured in the Flutter test VM on the build server (desktop CPU, in-memory stores, no platform channels). They were NOT measured on a phone. A phone CPU is several times slower and every store/vault call there is a platform-channel round trip, so the real gains should be larger than the ratios here, but that is a claim about the structure of the work, not a measurement. Reproduce with flutter test test/perf/privatepipelinebenchtest.dart (prints PERFMETRIC lines). What was found (by reading the code, then confirmed by the benchmarks) The bottom sheet itself was already fine: test/perf/sheetdragbuildstest.dart (existing) shows that dragging the People sheet rebuilds no rows. Roster updates are already coalesced to at most one per 220 ms (FamilyService.uiCoalesceWindow). The jank came from what ran on the UI isolate around the sheet in a Private circle: Cause Where Per received item 1 Every received fix rewrote the member's whole stored track (up to 6000 points: decode JSON, merge, sort, encode, write) PrivateHistory.add one rewrite 2 Every item read its circle key from the vault (Android Keystore decrypt behind a platform channel) ServiceChannelKeys -> E2eeService.circleKey one vault read 3 Pure-Dart XChaCha20/HKDF/Ed25519 on the UI isolate (cryptography without cryptographyflutter) ChannelReceiver.process ~5 ms on a desktop CPU 4 Receiver bookkeeping written per item (replay window of 512 seqs, high-water mark, epoch) ChannelReceiver.process 3 to 4 store writes 5 One map frame (and so one roster change, one coalescer entry) per item, also for catch-up items that are already outdated PrivateRuntime.apply one frame 6 replayLatest (runs on every members snapshot) decoded each member's whole 7 day track just to take the last point PrivateRuntime.replayLatest n/a 7 The upload queue was fully decoded three times per change (version check, write, read-back) SealedQueue.mutateOnce per own fix 8 OnDeviceProcessor (trip/drive/week) ran on every own fix, on the UI isolate, for every phone-only member PrivateRuntime.processOnDevice per own fix 9 A snapshot of the roster (REST or members frame) carries no positions in a Private circle, so every member showed "No location yet" until an async replay finished FamilyService.replaceMembers per snapshot On Android the preferences file is also re-read (SharedPreferences.reload(), every key, including the big track blobs) every 2 s and on every queue access; that cost grows with the size of the stored tracks. It is not changed here (see "Not done"). Benchmarks: before and after Scenario: Alice sends 300 fixes (10 s apart); Bob's phone catches up on them in one go (the "open the app after a while" case). Counting stores and a vault in the harness test/support/privatebenchharness.dart. Metric (Bob, 300 items) Before (0.23.0) After vault (Keystore) reads 300 1 key-value store reads 1803 12 key-value store writes 905 9 bytes written to the store 1,868,457 1,846 (plus one track write, below) bytes written, with a full 6000-point track already stored 68,424,556 (68 MB) 228,845 map frames / roster changes 300 2 wall time of the whole catch-up (inline crypto) 1771 ms 1532 ms wall time with a full 6000-point track 5363 ms 1589 ms replayLatest x10 with a 6000-point track 41 ms 1 ms Reading the table honestly: The crypto itself costs about the same (~5 ms per item here). It did not get faster; it was moved. In the app it now runs in a long-lived worker isolate (WorkerOpenRunner, itemopenjob.dart), so the UI isolate only does the cheap checks and the single apply per page. In the test VM the longest stretch the event loop was blocked during the catch-up fell to 21 ms with the worker (45 ms with the inline runner, which yields every 4 items). The "before" run cannot be compared on this metric: its event loop never yielded between items, so the probe timer never fired (maxLoopBlock=0 there means "the probe was starved", not "no blocking"). The big wins are I/O and rebuild counts: 300 -> 2 frames, 68 MB -> 0.2 MB written, 300 -> 1 Keystore reads. Sender side, 300 fixes sealed, queued and uploaded: 2742 ms (about 9 ms per fix, mostly the Ed25519 signature and the AEAD). No "before" figure was taken for this. The queue change (#7) removes two of the three full decodes per change; that is by construction, it is not separately benchmarked. What changed Receiver (privatechannel.dart): ChannelReceiver.processMany verifies a page in three stages: cheap checks and key/sender lookup (once per page), the heavy crypto as one hop to an OpenRunner, then the stateful checks (clock, replay window, epoch rollback, lane verdict) in order. Every check and its error mapping is unchanged; process is processMany of one. State is persisted once per batch. The same (device, seq) twice in one batch is refused as a duplicate. Tests: test/services/e2ee/ (unchanged, green) and privatepipelineregressiontest.dart (worker and inline runner give identical verdicts, including a flipped ciphertext byte and a duplicate). Small behaviour difference: for the legacy v1 item format the sender record is looked up before decrypting (v2 already did); a garbage item from an unknown device is now rejected as unknownSender instead of badCipher. Worker isolate (itemopenjob.dart): only plain bytes cross to the worker (key, ciphertext, sender public key); it starts on first use, stops after 30 s idle, and falls back to the calling isolate if it cannot start or times out. The key never leaves memory except as that message. Keys remembered (ServiceChannelKeys): found keys for 10 minutes, newest-epoch answers for 15 s, dropped when keys were synced (forgetKeys() for sign-out). Missing keys are never cached. History (PrivateHistory, writeBehind): new points wait in memory and are merged into the stored track once per 4 s / 400 points; reads and flushStores() (called when the app is paused) see them. The headless background isolate keeps the old write-at-once behaviour because it can be killed at any time. Catch-up apply (PrivateRuntime.applyBatch): fixes are grouped per member: one history write, one map frame with the newest fix. Older items of the page are in the history but are not replayed to the map. Upload queue (SealedQueue.head): the version/writer check reads the first two fields with a pattern instead of decoding the whole queue. Last known position (lastpositions.dart): the newest received position per member and circle is kept in the E2EE vault (Android Keystore wrapped, same as the circle keys), written 3 s after a change and when the app pauses, loaded once at start (PrivateRuntime.warmUp). It is never dropped for being old. replayLatest now reads it instead of the tracks; FamilyService.replaceMembers puts it on the roster immediately (synchronously) so a snapshot never flashes "No location yet". Heavy on-device processing is opt-in (see below). "Location not available" in Private mode: the cause and the wording Traced path: item -> ChannelReceiver -> PrivateRuntime.apply -> onMemberFrame -> FamilyService.applySealedLocation applyLocation -> Member -> memberStatusLine / MemberTile / PersonPanel. Every place that prints "No location yet" is gated on member.position == null (membertile.dart, memberstatus.dart, memberdetailscreen.dart, personpanel.dart, membermapper.dart, widgetsnapshot.dart). Ways a phone that does receive items still had a null position: 1. Roster snapshots wiped positions (cause 9): the server sends no positions for a Private circle, and the restore was an async replay that decoded whole tracks. Fixed (synchronous restore from memory). 2. Cold start was empty until a fresh item arrived or the track store was decoded. Fixed (vault-backed last position). 3. A frame for a member that is not yet in the roster is dropped (applyLocation returns when the id is unknown). The position is now in the last-position book and is applied when the roster arrives (withLastKnown). 4. When a silent member had a delivery hint (for example "has not received the circle key yet"), the hint replaced the age of the last position. Now the screen says both: "Kin's phone has not received the circle key yet · last seen 3 h ago" (memberStatusLine, memberDetailStatus). Older than 24 h the plain "Updates stopped" line says "last seen 2 d ago" instead of a clock time with no date. The reasons themselves still come from DeliveryHints (v0.22.2). 5. Items that are really refused (no key, unknown sender, old app) still give nothing to show; that is what the delivery hints explain. No code hides a member because the fix is old: the only staleness handling is the grey "stopped" status and the "Position from 3h ago" label (kStaleAfter = 10 minutes), the pin stays. Verified by reading the marker and list code (mapscreen.dart filters only on position != null). On-device reports are an opt-in switch, off by default Owner decision: a phone-only member's phone does only the light essentials by default (send its fix, receive and decrypt the others' latest fix, show the map). Trip, drive and weekly figures are not computed and no result item is sealed or sent until the member turns on "Compute driving reports on this phone" (My data processing screen, OnDeviceReportsTile). Setting key: OnDeviceReportsSetting.kvKey = procset/ondevicereports, value 1 = on. It lives in the private-circle store, i.e. the SharedPreferences key e2eechanprocset/ondevicereports (a file named after it on iOS), so the background location isolate reads the same value. Code: lib/services/processing/ondevicesetting.dart and lib/widgets/ondevicereportstile.dart (separate small files on purpose). When on: fixes are collected and processed in a batch at most every 60 s (onDeviceBatchEvery), yielding to the event loop every 20 fixes, and onDeviceAllowed can veto a batch (hook for "only while charging / battery not low"; not yet wired to a battery source). It still runs on the main isolate, not in a background isolate: the processor writes through the same stores as the rest of the runtime. Running it in an isolate was not done (see below). When off, the "Waiting for X's phone" card now ends with "Driving reports need the server: turn on the server for this circle, or X can enable phone reports." Server-assisted members are unaffected (the server computes for them). Startup and release configuration (checked, no change needed) Release APKs are built with flutter build apk --release (.github/workflows/apk.yml): AOT, no asserts. The app has one assert( and two print/debugPrint calls in lib/; nothing logs per item. PerfMonitor recording is off unless switched on (if (!recording) return;). main() awaits only the stored settings the first frame needs, read together (prefs step in PerfMonitor), and starts push registration and the config refresh after the first frame. The Private runtime does nothing before the first frame (warmUp is started from the map screen's initState, not awaited). Not done / could not verify Not measured on a phone. No Android device or emulator was available; all timings are test-VM timings. SharedPreferences.reload() cost (whole file, every 2 s and on every queue access) is unchanged. Moving the large track blobs out of preferences into files on Android was considered and not done: the headless background isolate has no custom platform channel on Android to find a directory, and a wrong fallback could split data. It is the most likely remaining source of lag on a phone with many members; a measurement on a device is the next step. cryptographyflutter (native crypto) was not added: it needs a native build that could not be verified here. The worker isolate removes the work from the UI isolate without it. Isolate for on-device reports, battery/charging gate: see above. Sealing of the phone's own fixes still happens on the UI isolate (about 9 ms per fix on a desktop CPU, one per few seconds).

docs.summary: Backend contract: docs/live-tracking.md (in the live-backend change). This page describes how the phone decides how often to read the GPS and post POST /locations, so a driving member's pin moves…
docs.text: Live tracking: the sending side (phone) Backend contract: docs/live-tracking.md (in the live-backend change). This page describes how the phone decides how often to read the GPS and post POST /locations, so a driving member's pin moves about once a second (Life360-style) while a parked phone stays as cheap as before. Code: File Role app/lib/services/trackingcadence.dart Pure policy (TrackingCadence, CadenceConfig, ProfileApplier) app/lib/services/fixquality.dart Bad-fix filter, speedmps / speedaccuracy fields app/lib/services/liveboost.dart liveboost command + "live": true parsing, cross-isolate boost + foreground-presence markers app/lib/services/locationreporter.dart Foreground reporter (map screen alive) app/lib/services/backgroundlocationservice.dart Background locator isolate app/packages/backgroundlocator2 Vendored plugin; new updateLocationRequest call Policy table Inputs: smoothed GPS speed, activity-recognition motion state, live boost, SOS burst, battery, foreground vs background. Precedence: SOS > boost > driving > walking > stationary. Tier Entered when GPS request Post gate (min between POSTs) stationary, foreground default stream, distanceFilter 10 m 5 s idle (background, same spot 10 min) balanced power interval 3 min, distanceFilter 30 m 10 s stationary, background default interval 60 s, filter 0 (native drops to the 15 min STILL profile when activity recognition says still, liveness alarm unchanged) 10 s walking smoothed speed >= 0.8 m/s, or motion state walking/running/cycling/driving 5 s, filter 0 5 s driving smoothed speed >= 3 m/s for 2 consecutive fixes, or one fix >= 8 m/s 1 s, filter 0 850 ms (GPS request is 1 Hz, so never above 1 Hz) boosted liveboost command or "live": true response 1 s, filter 0 850 ms SOS SOS burst (5 min) 2 s, filter 0 2 s (unchanged from before) Exits (hysteresis): driving ends after smoothed speed stays below 1 m/s for 60 s (red lights and traffic keep drive mode; speeds between 1 and 3 m/s never end it); walking ends after 30 s with speed below 0.4 m/s and no moving motion state; boost ends at its TTL (capped at 120 s); each "live": true response extends it by 10 s; no fix for 120 s resets the speed history and returns to the slow profile. Low battery: below 15 % and not charging, and not boosted / SOS: walking becomes 15 s and driving 5 s. Stationary is unchanged. All numbers are constants in CadenceConfig. Applying the profile Foreground: LocationReporter re-opens the geolocator stream (interval via AndroidSettings.intervalDuration, distanceFilter) when the GPS part of the profile changes. A 5 s timer re-evaluates so a boost/SOS expiry or a drive-mode exit is applied even when the distance-filtered stream is silent. Background: the isolate calls the new native BackgroundLocator.updateLocationRequest(intervalMs, distanceFilter, highAccuracy), which re-requests location updates inside the running foreground service (no service restart). Fast requests (<= 10 s) always run as requested; slow requests keep the native STILL low-power profile when activity recognition says the device is still. If the call is unavailable (older native build) the isolate falls back to a full re-registration. Debounce: a GPS-request change is applied at most every 20 s (minApplyGap). Speeding up for boost or SOS bypasses the debounce. A non-stationary profile is re-sent every 5 min in case native state was reset. The service keeps using the existing foreground notification while driving. Not piling up requests One POST in flight per reporter. A fix arriving meanwhile becomes the single pending fix; the pending fix it replaces is written to LocationOutbox and ships through POST /locations/batch (drains are throttled to every 10 s). While the app is open and its own reporter is alive (it marks a shared timestamp every 5 s), the background isolate skips fast-tier posts so the backend does not receive two 1 Hz streams. Fix quality and speed Before sending, fixes are dropped when: timestamp is not newer than the last accepted / sent one; accuracy > 50 m while moving (> 1 m/s); or the jump from the previous accepted fix implies > 70 m/s (after 3 consecutive such fixes the new position becomes the baseline, e.g. tunnel exit). speedmps is the receiver's speed, including 0 when the GPS says 0 and horizontal accuracy is <= 30 m (0 with worse accuracy may mean "no speed" and is omitted). speedaccuracy (m/s) is sent when the platform reports a positive value. Speeds above 120 m/s are dropped. Live boost Direct push command {"type":"liveboost","ttls":60} is handled in DirectPushDispatcher (either isolate; the deadline is also persisted in shared preferences so the other isolate picks it up within ~5 s). Missing / invalid ttls defaults to 60 s; the TTL is capped at 120 s. POST /locations responses with "live": true keep the boost alive. Viewer side: ApiClient.watchMember(userId, {circleId}) and the no-throw ApiClient.watchMemberQuiet call POST /locations/watch (the map should call it about every 15 s while a member is on screen). Coordinates are never logged. Diagnostics The Performance screen's "Copy report" includes a location reporting: line with the active cadence profile and fixes sent (this / last minute). Only the foreground reporter reports there; the background isolate has no UI. Tuning / battery notes Driving at 1 Hz costs noticeably more battery than the previous 60 s cadence, but only while speed >= 3 m/s or someone is watching. The outbox holds 720 points (12 minutes at 1 Hz) if the phone is offline while driving. Idle tier (battery saver) In the background, once the device has stayed within 60 m of the same spot for 10 minutes with no walking, driving or moving activity evidence, the profile relaxes to idle: balanced-power accuracy, a 3 minute interval and a 30 m displacement filter. Reporting never stops (the 10 minute heartbeat and the interval keep running). Any fix more than 60 m from the anchor, walking-or-faster speed, a moving activity state, a live boost or SOS leaves idle at once. Fixes without coordinates never count as stillness. The foreground reporter never uses it. iOS has no interval: every tier is mapped to a Core Location accuracy and distance filter, and idle becomes a cell-only "still" request with a 150 m exit region. Table, thresholds and the iPhone test plan: iOS background location. Battery comparison procedure (physical device only) Emulators cannot measure this. The adaptive policy (trackingcadence.dart: still / walking / driving profiles, low-battery intervals at <= 15%, idle back-off after 10 minutes within 60 m) has no measured numbers yet; record them with this procedure and paste results here. 1. Same phone, fully charged, screen off, same mobile network, battery saver off, adb shell dumpsys batterystats --reset before each run. 2. Run A, fixed interval: a build with CadenceConfig forced to the walking profile (5 s GPS) for 8 hours of a normal day (home/commute/work). 3. Run B, adaptive: the shipping build over the same route/schedule. 4. After each: adb bugreport or dumpsys batterystats --charged; note percentage drained, GPS wake time and number of POST /locations. 5. Record freshness: the 95th percentile age of the last fix while moving (must stay under ~10 s) and while still (under ~3 min).

headings.text: Why it used to look jumpy

docs.text: Live tracking: the viewer side (smooth map, follow, speed) Counterpart of docs/live-tracking.md (backend and reporter contract). This page covers what the map does with the fixes it receives. None of it could be run on a device while writing it; the unit and widget tests use a fake clock. Why it used to look jumpy A pin jumped to every fix as it arrived (roughly every 2-10 s), the caption rounded the speed to a whole mph from whatever the last roster said, and tapping a member only animated the camera once. Now the pin is animated every frame from a per-member track, the camera can lock onto it, and the speed is the freshest GPS speed with a short low-pass. Pieces File Role app/lib/services/markermotion.dart Pure Dart per-member smoother (MarkerMotion, TrackFix, MotionSample, MotionConfig). app/lib/services/membermotionhub.dart Owns one MarkerMotion per member; frames (per animation frame) and speeds (per fix) notifiers. app/lib/services/followcamera.dart Locks the map camera to a member's display position, one MapController.move per frame. app/lib/services/watchclient.dart POST /locations/watch every 15 s while looking at someone. app/lib/screens/mapscreen.dart One Ticker, the follow pill, marker layer. No setState per frame. app/lib/widgets/livespeed.dart LiveSpeedBuilder: rebuilds just a speed text per fix and on unit change. How the smoother works Time is always passed in (DateTime now), so it is deterministic in tests. 1. Render about one fix behind. When a fix arrives the pin eases from where it is drawn now to the fix over the fix-to-fix interval (the ts delta, clamped to 0.5-2.5 s, default 1 s). A steady 1 Hz drive becomes constant-velocity motion; chained segments are linear, a pin that was at rest eases out so it does not lurch. 2. Coast when the next fix is late. After the segment ends the pin keeps going along the heading at the GPS speed for up to 3 s (constant for 2 s, then tapering to a stop), then holds. Only when the speed is fresh and above 0.5 m/s. 3. Never backwards. If a late fix lands behind the coasting pin, the pin holds until the track overtakes it. 4. Snap, don't glide, on teleports: a jump over 500 m, a gap over 2 min, or the first fix. 5. Jitter rejection: a stationary fix (speed < 0.5 m/s) within max(accuracy, 8 m) of the pin is ignored for position (speed, heading and time are still taken), so a parked pin does not wander. 6. Out-of-order or duplicate fixes (ts not newer than the newest) are dropped. 7. Heading (headingdeg, or the track bearing when absent) is trusted only while moving, held otherwise, and smoothed on the shortest arc with a 0.25 s time constant (359 -> 1 turns 2 degrees, not 358). 8. Speed: the freshest speedmps, 3-sample low-pass (rising: 75 % newest; falling: weighted mean 0.5/0.3/0.2). Exactly 0 below 0.5 m/s or when the fix is older than 15 s or was already old when first loaded. 0 is a value; null (no speed in the fix) shows as an em dash. Display uses UnitPreferenceService.units (mph or km/h). "Speeding" is round(mph) >= 70, i.e. the number on screen. Constants (MotionConfig) minSegmentS 0.5, maxSegmentS 2.5, defaultSegmentS 1.0, deadReckonMaxS 3.0, teleportMeters 500, teleportGapS 120, stationaryMps 0.5, stationaryMinRadiusM 8, headingTauS 0.25, speedStaleS 15, maxPlausibleMps 90. Frame cost One Ticker in MapScreen. It runs only while a pin or the follow glide needs frames and stops itself when everything has settled, so an idle map and a tab switch cost 0 frames and 0 rebuilds. The ticker is muted by TickerMode when the map tab or route is hidden. Each tick calls MemberMotionHub.tick(), which notifies only the marker layer; it setStates itself, not the screen. The marker layer reuses its cached bubbles and its clustering result. It re-clusters only when the roster, camera, expanded set or followed member change, or when a moving member drifted over 24 px since the last clustering. The followed member is never clustered. The speed caption inside a cached bubble listens to hub.speeds itself, so the bubble is not rebuilt when the number changes. PerfMonitor counters: MarkerFrame and MapMarkerLayer rebuilds (with "Record details" on) and map animation frames. Guards: app/test/perf/livemotiontest.dart (host never rebuilds, bubbles not rebuilt, clustering not per frame, idle = 0) and the existing shelltabswitchtest.dart / markerlayertest.dart. Follow mode Tapping a member marker or a People row centers on them and locks the camera to their display position every frame (MapController.move, no animation stacking). The first 450 ms glide eases onto the member; the zoom is kept unless it is below 14, then 16. Any user pan, pinch or fling (hasGesture) releases the lock. The pill "Following Name" stays with a recenter button (re-follow) and an X (stop). Tapping the name opens the member's details. Follow state lives in MapScreen's state, so it survives rebuilds, the member leaving the viewport, and style/satellite toggles. It stops when the member goes offline (status stopped, no position, left the roster) or when the user uses Locate me or expands a cluster. While following (even if the user has panned away and the pill is showing), the app calls POST /locations/watch immediately and then every 15 s (server TTL is 45 s) so the target's phone reports at about 1 Hz. Calls stop when following ends, the app is backgrounded, or the map is hidden (TickerMode). Failures are silent: the target just keeps its normal cadence. Not done / needs a device Rotating the pin arrow to headingdeg while driving is not implemented (the smoothed heading is available as MotionSample.headingDeg). Real frame times, how it feels at 1 Hz over cellular, and the end-to-end watch boost with the reporter agent were not run on hardware.

docs.title: Live tracking (Life360-style moving pin)
docs.summary: Contract between the backend and the Flutter reporter/map. All changes are additive; old clients keep working.
docs.text: Live tracking (Life360-style moving pin) Contract between the backend and the Flutter reporter/map. All changes are additive; old clients keep working. Data flow 1. Reporter (driving, or while "watched") sends a fix every ~1-2 s: POST /locations (Bearer or X-Device-Key). 2. Server validates, stores the fix (moving fixes are never deduplicated), upserts memberpositions (never moves backwards), returns 201. 3. After commit, the server broadcasts a location WebSocket frame to every connected member who may see the reporter (circle membership + sharing enabled, evaluated per frame). 4. Map clients interpolate between frames using ts, speedmps, headingdeg. 5. Offline backlog: POST /locations/batch (history only, no WS frames). Frame: WS location {"type":"location","userid":"<uuid>","lat":1.0,"lon":2.0, "ts":"2026-01-01T12:00:00Z","lastseenat":"2026-01-01T12:00:01Z", "batterypct":80,"speedmps":13.4,"headingdeg":271.5, "motionstate":"driving","accuracymeters":6.0,"circleid":"<uuid, optional>"} ts: GPS fix time (use for interpolation); lastseenat: server receipt. speedmps, headingdeg (degrees clockwise from north), accuracymeters, batterypct, motionstate: nullable (null/absent when unknown). headingdeg is also in the members snapshot (WS members frame and GET /family/members), nullable. placepresence (members snapshot and GET /family/members only, not location frames; omitted when unknown or location-hidden): {"placeid","placename", "state":"at""left","since":"<RFC3339>"}, derived from the latest geofence enter/exit events (no extra storage). "at" = arrived at since and not yet exited; "left" = last exit at since. Powers "At Home since 3:42 PM" / "Left Work 25 min ago". A fix whose ts is not newer than the stored position is rejected (400) on POST /locations, so the pin never moves backwards. Stationary dedup (unchanged intent) A fix is collapsed (HTTP 200 {"status":"deduplicated","ts":...,"live":bool}, a presence frame instead of location) only when it is within 10 m of the stored position AND speedmps is absent or <= 1.5. Any fix with speedmps > 1.5 or moved = 10 m (radius widens to the fix's own accuracymeters, capped at 25 m, when it is worse than 10 m) is stored and broadcast every time. Rate limits POST /locations: 300 per minute per user (5 Hz sustained headroom; 1 Hz needs 60). Runaway loops still get 429. POST /locations/batch: 60 per minute per user, up to 500 points each. POST /locations/watch: 30 per minute per user (1 call per ~15 s is normal). Watch / live boost Viewer opens the map on a member and calls every ~15 s while looking: POST /locations/watch {"userid":"<target uuid>","circleid":"<optional uuid>"} Response 200: {"status":"watching","ttls":45,"boost":true} Authorization is identical to reading the target's location: the viewer must share a circle with the target and the target must be sharing with the viewer (and, if circleid is given, in that circle). Otherwise 404 (member not found) - no probing. Self-watch returns 200 with {"status":"self"} and does nothing. The watch lapses 45 s after the last call. While at least one watch is live, the target is "boosted". When a boost starts (or restarts after lapsing), the server sends the target's devices one direct push (SSE /push/stream, same channel as locationrequest; also UnifiedPush/APNs silent fallbacks): {"type":"liveboost","ttls":60} At most one command per target per 30 s regardless of watcher count. While watches keep renewing, the command is re-sent about every 45 s (ttl 60 s) so a push-only device stays boosted. It carries NO coordinates and no viewer identity. Foreground reporters without push learn the state from the ingest response: POST /locations 201 and 200 (deduplicated) bodies gain "live": true while boosted (omitted/false otherwise). Reporter should send every ~1-2 s while live is true or liveboost was received (until ttl), else its normal cadence. Privacy rationale Boost only exists while someone with permission is actively looking (watch TTL 45 s, renewed by the viewer's open map). A member who paused sharing cannot be boosted; the server also refuses. Push payloads never contain position. State is in memory only; a restart simply ends boosts. Hot path notes (per accepted fix) Database round trips for POST /locations (moving fix): 1 transaction = BEGIN, device-ownership check + user row lock (one statement), last-position read, locations INSERT, then memberpositions upsert + device heartbeat pipelined in one round trip, COMMIT. The audit-log row is written at most once per user per minute. After the ack, the WebSocket broadcast costs ONE query (own + sharing circles via OwnAndSharingCircles) and no per-viewer queries; geofence evaluation runs asynchronously on a bounded worker pool. Measured BenchmarkIngestMoving (backend/internal/handlers/livetest.go, real TimescaleDB pg16 in Docker on a heavily loaded shared host, 1000-fix runs): about 8 ms per moving-fix POST /locations (full handler, including commit), i.e. one core could sustain >100 fixes/s; 1 Hz x several members is negligible. Before replacing the users ... FOR UPDATE row lock with a per-user advisory lock the same benchmark measured ~280 ms/op on the same host (the row lock dirtied the hot users page and forced a WAL write per fix). Run: TESTDATABASEURL=... go test ./internal/handlers -run x -bench IngestMoving.

docs.title: Relationship to the original project
docs.summary: Orbitly here is an independently maintained continuation of wheresfrank/openfamily (AGPL-3.0). It started from that project's history, which is preserved in this repository, and has since diverged…
docs.text: Relationship to the original project Orbitly here is an independently maintained continuation of wheresfrank/openfamily (AGPL-3.0). It started from that project's history, which is preserved in this repository, and has since diverged substantially. Nothing depends on upstream No git remote, workflow, updater, container image, release asset or APK download in this repository points at the original repository. The in-app and server update paths use this repository's own signed releases. The old Docker-socket updater was removed. There is no automatic synchronization. Do not enable "Sync fork". Reviewing upstream changes by hand (optional) git remote add upstream https://github.com/wheresfrank/openfamily.git git fetch upstream git log --oneline main..upstream/main # what they changed git diff main...upstream/main -- path/ # inspect before porting anything git cherry-pick <sha> # port a single fix if you want it git remote remove upstream # when done Port changes deliberately and test them. Keep the AGPL notices and the NOTICE attribution intact when copying code.

docs.title: Performance
docs.summary: The server is not the bottleneck (/healthz ~1.5 ms locally, hot endpoints below 15 ms p95 on a seeded database; see "Backend"). The work here targets the phone: rebuild cost, startup, and request…

headings.text: Before / after (measured in tests, same harness on `main` and here)

docs.text: Performance The server is not the bottleneck (/healthz ~1.5 ms locally, hot endpoints below 15 ms p95 on a seeded database; see "Backend"). The work here targets the phone: rebuild cost, startup, and request count. None of it could be run on a device while writing it, so this page also describes how to collect real numbers. On-device instrumentation Open Settings, tap the "Orbitly / Version" row 7 times (each tap within 2 s of the last). The hidden Performance screen shows: startup: process start to first frame (process age at main() from /proc/self/stat, plus main() to first frame) and timed startup steps; frame build and raster p50 / p90 / p99, janky-frame percentage against the display refresh rate (16.7 ms at 60 Hz, 8.3 ms at 120 Hz), and the 10 slowest frames with the screen that was visible (AppShell:location, a page class name, ...); per-screen rebuild counters (MapScreen, LocationTabView, PeopleList, PersonRow, MapMarkers, MapMarkerLayer); WebSocket frames received / applied / UI updates, total and per minute; HTTP requests and latency by endpoint (ring buffer of the last 400). Copy report puts a compact text report on the clipboard; Reset clears the counters. Only a tiny always-on frame summary runs by default (one FrameTiming callback, fixed-size histograms). Rebuilds, HTTP and WebSocket recorders are off until "Record details" is switched on. Everything is in memory: nothing is written to disk or sent anywhere. HTTP entries are METHOD /normalised/path only: ids, tokens, queries, bodies and coordinates never reach the buffer (path segments that are not plain lower-case words become :id). Code: app/lib/services/perf/perfmonitor.dart, app/lib/screens/performancescreen.dart. Collecting numbers 1. Install a release or profile build, open the Performance screen, switch on "Record details", Reset, then use the app for a few minutes (open the map, drag the sheet, switch tabs, open a trip report, let a family member drive). 2. Copy report and send it. 3. Cross-checks without the app: adb shell dumpsys gfxinfo app.openfamily reset then use the app, then adb shell dumpsys gfxinfo app.openfamily framestats (per-frame timestamps; "Janky frames" and the 50/90/95/99th percentiles are at the top of plain dumpsys gfxinfo app.openfamily). Cold start: adb shell am start -W -n app.openfamily/.MainActivity (TotalTime). Flutter DevTools: flutter run --profile, open the Performance tab (frame chart, "Track widget rebuilds"), the CPU profiler, and the Network tab. Use a profile build, never debug, for timings. What changed Area Change Map / sheet A WebSocket location frame no longer rebuilds MapScreen, the tab view, the tile layer or the sheet. The roster is a ValueNotifier that only the range circles, the marker layer and the People list listen to. Hidden tabs and covered routes skip those rebuilds (VisibleValueBuilder, keyed on TickerMode). Burst coalescing FamilyService delivers live frames to the UI at most once per 220 ms (leading edge immediate, trailing delivery with the newest data). Snapshots (REST, members frame, circle switch) are never delayed. Markers Bubble widgets are cached per member instance, so panning only recomputes positions. Tile layer sits in its own RepaintBoundary and is a const widget. People rows A row widget is reused while its member and flags are unchanged. Floating buttons The Check in / SOS / layers row is a ValueListenableBuilder child, not rebuilt on every sheet drag frame. Avatars Decoded at 2x display size with ResizeImage (was native size); a cached photo is in the first frame (no initials flash); decode is precached when the bytes land. Shell Tab bodies are created once; switching tabs no longer rebuilds every visited tab. Startup main() reads theme, map style and server URL in parallel and does not await the system-UI call. The session gate runs housekeeping, the /config fetch and the session check together. Push sync and the config refresh start after the first frame. Network /config cached 5 min and single-flighted; places cached 30 s (invalidated on create / update / delete / login / logout, bypassed by the Places screen); roster and places fetched side by side; family name and roster fetched together; the circles screen return no longer fetches /circles twice. JSON Responses of 128 KB or more are decoded with compute(). WebSocket Backoff resets only after a connection survived 10 s (was: on the first frame, so accept-then-drop servers were retried every second); connectivity events are debounced 800 ms. Audited and left alone: saveLayer sources (no BackdropFilter, ShaderMask, ColorFiltered, ImageFiltered or antiAliasWithSaveLayer anywhere; five Opacity / AnimatedOpacity uses that only layer while dimmed or fading, guarded by test/perf/savelayeraudittest.dart); no shrinkWrap lists; long lists are already lazy; no per-second tickers (labels are clock times); the vector tile layer stays mounted (dropping it would blank the map on every return to the Location tab, and while hidden it does no work now) with its existing 2 concurrent / 10 MB / 50 MB settings and a style future that is only recreated when the style URL changes. Considered and not done: showing the shell before the session check finishes. The check refreshes the token over the network when the 15-minute access token expired; running that in parallel with the first API calls would race two refreshes on the same refresh token. It needs the gate's refresh and the 401 refresh unified into one single-flight first. Behaviour changes /config is reused for 5 minutes (was refetched on resume); places for 30 s outside the Places screen. Live location frames reach the map at most ~4.5 times per second. The Driving / Circle tabs still update only on roster snapshots, exactly as before (the shared notifier keeps its identity semantics). WebSocket backoff reset and connectivity debounce, as above. Session gate: legacy cleanup no longer precedes the config fetch and session check (they run concurrently). Before / after (measured in tests, same harness on main and here) Proxy Before After Requests at startup (gate + map + push) 7 (/config x3) 5 Requests on resume / pull-to-refresh 3 (members, places, config) 1 Requests on circle switch 2 1 20 location frames: tab view rebuilds 20 0 20 location frames: person rows rebuilt 200 20 20 location frames: DsListRow builds 220 40 50 frames in 1 s: UI updates 50 6 20 tab switches (4 tabs visited): body rebuilds 80 0 30 pan frames, 6 members: bubble rebuilds 90 0 40 sheet-drag frames: floating buttons rebuilt 80 0 4000x3000 avatar at 44 dp, 3x: decoded bitmap 46,875 KB 204 KB 2.5 MB JSON: longest event-loop gap 76 ms (sync decode) 55 ms Hidden Location tab, 20 frames: row rebuilds not measured on main (it had no hidden-tab guard) 0 The JSON row is a weak result on a loaded x86 host: the gap includes isolate start-up and result hand-over, so treat the benefit on a phone as unconfirmed until measured. The numbers come from flutter test output lines starting PERFMETRIC (see test/perf, test/services/startuprequeststest.dart). Frame times, startup time and jank percentage cannot be measured in tests; use the Performance screen. Backend backend/internal/handlers/perfendpointstest.go (opt-in: OFPERF=1 and TESTDATABASEURL, throwaway database only) seeds 3 users, 20,000 locations, 300 trips, 1,020 trip events and 5 places on TimescaleDB, then times each endpoint 40 times through the real handlers (handler plus Postgres, no network): Endpoint p50 p95 GET /config 0.01 ms 0.04 ms GET /family/members 2.6 ms 7.0 ms GET /family/places 1.0 ms 1.2 ms GET /trips (30 days, limit 200) 1.8 ms 3.1 ms GET /trips/report (week) 6.4 ms 9.4 ms GET /trips/report (month) 7.9 ms 13.7 ms GET /trips/{id} 1.6 ms 4.0 ms POST /locations 5.3 ms 10.6 ms Everything is far below 100 ms, so no index or migration was added. Measure on the phone See the checklist in the pull-request description; in short: cold start time, janky % and p99 while dragging the sheet and panning with 3+ members, rebuild counts and WebSocket UI updates per minute during a drive, and the HTTP table after launch and after switching circle.

docs.title: Real-server interop test of the processing lanes
docs.summary: scripts/e2e-lanes.sh proves that the real Dart phone code (app/lib/services/e2ee/, LanesService, PrivateRuntime, ApiClient) works against the real Go server in backend/, instead of only against the…
docs.text: Real-server interop test of the processing lanes scripts/e2e-lanes.sh proves that the real Dart phone code (app/lib/services/e2ee/, LanesService, PrivateRuntime, ApiClient) works against the real Go server in backend/, instead of only against the in-memory fake (app/test/support/fakee2eeserver.dart). Docker only. The script builds the server, e2ee-bridge and a tiny SQL probe (copied temporarily to backend/cmd/e2eprobe, removed again) in golang:1.27, starts a throwaway TimescaleDB (fsync=off) and the server (host network, ports E2EDBPORT=55433, E2EAPIPORT=18089), then runs flutter test test/e2erealserver/ in ghcr.io/cirruslabs/flutter:stable. Containers have unique names and are removed at the end. Extra arguments are passed to flutter test. scripts/e2e-lanes.sh E2EREQUIRESIDECAR=1 scripts/e2e-lanes.sh # also fail while the sidecar predates lanes E2EBUILTIN=1 scripts/e2e-lanes.sh test/e2erealserver/builtine2etest.dart # no sidecar: the API is its own server device E2ERUN=dev E2EKEEP=1 scripts/e2e-lanes.sh # keep the stack between runs (development) Without E2EBASEURL (the normal flutter test) the suite is skipped. How the pieces fit: ApiClient insists on https and one token store, so the tests use a pretend https host that a zone-scoped http client rewrites to the real server and signs with the token of the phone the call belongs to. The Orbitly server's own device is the real e2ee-bridge binary (enroll --kind server, approved by the admin phone through approveLinkRequest, pinned by run). Plaintext at the server is checked in the database (locations, memberpositions) through the probe, and the server log is grepped for Cleo's coordinates by the script. Scenarios (app/test/e2erealserver/lanese2etest.dart): policy, lanes in use (Anna, Ben server; Cleo phone), the real sidecar, cross reading and badges, opt-out, requiredserver, an app without the lanes capability, and a circle key handed out as the server key. Encrypted chat scenario app/test/e2erealserver/chate2etest.dart runs in the same stack (scripts/e2e-lanes.sh test/e2erealserver/chate2etest.dart): three phones exchange sealed chat, edit, delete (author and admin, plus a member's forged edit/delete that must change nothing), a photo, a removed member, and a member in the server lane whose chat still goes on the phone line while the real sidecar runs. The database is searched for the message words (e2eeitems, chatmessages, auditlog, photo blobs) and the script greps the server log for them at the end. Plaintext send answers 409 chatencrypted. Offline scenario (server stopped mid-test) app/test/e2erealserver/offlinee2etest.dart (run it on its own: scripts/e2e-lanes.sh test/e2erealserver/offlinee2etest.dart) proves the store-and-forward path against the real server. The script runs a small control loop next to the tests (E2ECTLDIR, mounted at /ctl): the test writes stop or start to /ctl/request and the script stops or starts the API container, answering in /ctl/ack. Anna's phone sends a chat message, the server is stopped, and her phone keeps queuing three more messages, a check-in and an SOS (real refused connections, no fakes), failed flushes lose nothing, the queue is "killed" and re-read from storage, the server is started, and everything arrives once and in order. Replaying the same client ids (a lost answer) changes nothing: the database is queried for exactly one check-in, one SOS and the four messages in order. See docs/design/OFFLINERESILIENCE.md.
